stages.owner: The rest of the grenade shipment had been stashed around the city. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the charges and fuses that are stored in these <Col: StageText>boxes</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers have found our box of grenade casings. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up this box </Col>of fuses.

stages.owner: The last part of the grenade shipment contains the pins and pull rings. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>case </Col>here. Without them, the gangs may as well be throwing stones.
stages.dispatch: Enforcers have confiscated all but one of the components from our grenade shipment. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>retrieving the case </Col>full of pins and pull rings.

stages.owner: Great Work! <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>those deadly <Col: StageText>components </Col>at our <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>, so they can be melted down into promotional CSA paperclips or something.
stages.dispatch: All our grenade components have been taken by the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the shipment </Col>to their lockup. Make the 'Forcers go - boom!

stages.owner: The Criminals obviously still need their frag fix. They want to steal replacement grenades from our supplies. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col>. Don't they know: never touch another dude's pineapple.
stages.dispatch: There are easier ways to get hold of grenades - like stealing them from the Enforcers! <Col: StageText>Force your way in </Col>to their supply depot. We need those grenades.
There are easier ways to get hold of grenades - like stealing them from the Enforcers! <Col: StageText>Force your way in </Col>to their supply depot. We need those grenades.

stages.owner: They've raided one of our supply depots! <Col:StageText>Retreive the weapons</Col> and drop them off at the secure location.
stages.dispatch: There's more than just grenades here! Take the weapons back to the <Col:StageText>drop-off</Col>. You'll be handsomely rewarded.
There's more than just grenades here! Take the weapons back to the <Col:StageText>drop-off</Col>. You'll be handsomely rewarded.

stages.owner: Lonny Dorengo came over here from the Concession and has been cutting himself into the action - hitting gangs as much as cops and 'Forcers. He's planning a meeting. <Col: StageText>Plant bugs in the area</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Lonny Dorengo came here from the Concession, and has been hitting up gangs and 'Forcers alike. We're gonna deal with him, but need privacy for the hit - <Col: StageText>stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>bugging these payphones</Col>.

stages.owner: Lonny Dorengo ain't particularly stable - he'll pull shit on anyone with gold, drugs or cash. Needless to say he ain't got many friends left. <Col: StageText>Plant a bug on his window</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Lonny Dorengo ain't stable - he'll pull shit on anyone with gold, drugs or cash. You can imagine how much we hate his guts. <Col: StageText>Stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>bugging this shop front </Col>so we can kill him discreetly.

stages.owner: Just in case Lonny gives his "You see Derren's face on this dollar? I wipe my ass on it" speech, <Col: StageText>plant a bug on this ATM</Col>. That should cover enough of the area to overhear anything talked about.
stages.dispatch: This is always the problem when you want to do a hit - no fucking privacy. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>bugging this ATM</Col>. Lonny Dorengo has to die today!

stages.owner: We've got a listening post set up. <Col: StageText>Head there and wait </Col>until we hear something we can use. Lonny's on the way, driving that big-ass car of his.
stages.dispatch: Lonny thinks we've built up our loot again after his last raid - he's on the way to claim it. We gotta kill him now, so <Col: StageText>stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>getting to their bug-listening post</Col>.

stages.owner: Lonny's pretty excited - a gang he fucked over last week has rebuilt their stash. <Col: StageText>Pick up the stash </Col>before he gets to it. Meanwhile, we're gonna bust every last one of these mofos for racketeering.
stages.dispatch: Lonny Dorengo is dead! Unfortunately, the 'Forcer surveillance squad heard the whole thing, and are coming to bust us. No love there, then. <Col: StageText>Recover the bag of loot </Col>we used to bait Dorengo.

stages.owner: That loot was bait to get Lonny out in the open. His own gang and the target gang both turned on him. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the bag of <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to the <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>. Make sure Criminals don't get hold of the bag.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Deliver the bag of loot </Col>back to our hideout and make sure the Enforcers don't get hold of it. With Lonny out of the way, we ought to be able to build up a much larger stash.

stages.owner: That loot was bait to get Lonny out in the open. His own gang and the target gang both turned on him. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the bag of <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to the <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>. Make sure Criminals don't get hold of the bag.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Deliver the bag of loot </Col>back to our hideout and make sure the Enforcers don't get hold of it. With Lonny out of the way, we ought to be able to build up a much larger stash.

stages.owner: Our CSA license allows us to carry out private security work, and a few of our clients need cash to be picked up and delivered. <Col: StageText>Collect the armored truck </Col>we'll use to transport the money.
stages.dispatch: Several business owners want to avoid paying us protection by using Enforcers to transport their daily takings. Bad idea. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the security truck </Col>they use.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>and keep it safe. Like a lot of places in San Paro, this neighborhood has some bad elements, so make sure you keep the money out of Criminal hands.
stages.dispatch: I hear those business owners will be transporting a lot of money - in this neighborhood, that could easily go missing. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the cash</Col>.

stages.owner: Nice work! That's why we've always had satisfied clients. Now <Col: StageText>drop off the money </Col>to its destination.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are going to drop off those bags of cash. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the money </Col>and completing their contract.

stages.owner: Welcome to the crazy world of private security: one of our clients just dropped their money en route to the pick-up. Klutz. <Col: StageText>Search this area </Col>and see if you can <Col: StageText>recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>bag of cash</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Lucky us! The Enforcers were doing one last pick-up, but a klutz shop assistant dropped the money on the way. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>searching this area </Col>for the missing money.

stages.owner: Good job - all the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>has been picked up and accounted for. <Col: StageText>Drop it off </Col>here, and don't let any Criminals get hold of it.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are going to drop off that <Col: StageText>bag of cash</Col>. Stop them. <Col: StageText>Deliver it </Col>back to our hideout instead. Meanwhile, we'll double the protection payments for those shop owners!

stages.owner: Good job - all the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>has been picked up and accounted for. <Col: StageText>Drop it off </Col>here, and don't let any Criminals get hold of it.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are going to drop off that <Col: StageText>bag of cash</Col>. Stop them. <Col: StageText>Deliver it </Col>back to our hideout instead. Meanwhile, we'll double the protection payments for those shop owners!

stages.owner: We know that the gangs collect their account sheets at this time of year. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>their accountant's <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and get that vital <Col: StageText>information</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians have targeted our accountant to see where we're earning our money. Make sure they don't get hold of the <Col: StageText>account sheets </Col>he has in his car.

stages.owner: The gangs use drop-off points to relay their financial information. If we <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>their <Col: StageText>account sheets </Col>first, we'll get a valuable overview of their organization.
stages.dispatch: 'Torians are collecting financial intel on our organization. <Col: StageText>Stop 'em </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the <Col: StageText>account sheets</Col>. They'll only be jealous of our wealth, anyway.

stages.owner: The final set of <Col: StageText>account sheets </Col>was left for <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>here. Don't even bother trying to read 'em, though: you'll fall asleep on the job.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians have gathered most of the financial files they need to make a case against us. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the last of the <Col: StageText>accounts</Col>.

stages.owner: Get those <Col: StageText>account sheets </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>them back here now. We'll be able to examine every element of the gang's business.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians have a wealth of evidence against us now. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>bringing </Col>the <Col: StageText>account sheets </Col>back to their <Col: StageText>lockup</col>.

stages.owner: Another successful Praetorian case, and the gangs don't like it! You'd think they'd be proud of their 'figures'. They'll attempt to save face by controlling this corner. Go <Col: StageText>secure the area</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians won't be able to use that financial evidence against us if they can't present it in person. Prevent that - <Col: StageText>control this corner</Col> to scare off any possible jurors; extreme prejudice encouraged.

stages.owner: A Tiger's deep undercover in a local gang. He's gonna leave details of their armaments for us, hiding them in normal looking packages. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the first set of <Col: StageText>intel files </Col>from this <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>.
stages.dispatch: I suspect the Tigers are being sold info on our armaments. I made a dummy <Col: StageText>document </Col> and left it in this vehicle. See if its location gets leaked. If anyone tries to collect it, <Col: StageText>stop them</Col> .

stages.owner: The next set of <Col: StageText>intel files </Col>was left for <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>at this address. Nothing concrete in these reports yet.
stages.dispatch: We need to find out who is leaking our plans to the Prentiss Tigers. In the meantime, <Col: StageText>stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>more <Col: StageText>files </Col>on us.

stages.owner: The last set of <Col: StageText>intel files </Col>from our inside guy was left for <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>at this address. Hopefully they'll give us an idea of the gang's offensive capabilities.
stages.dispatch: We're closing in on our mole, but they're still evading us for now. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the last of the <Col: StageText>files </Col>that have been leaked.

stages.owner: You've got all the <Col: StageText>intel files</Col>. <Col: StageText>Drop them off </Col>at this Tiger safe house.
stages.dispatch: We've plugged our leak - permanently - but the Tigers already have a lot of information. Stop them from getting the intel <Col: StageText>files </Col>back to their <Col: StageText>lockup</col>.

stages.owner: The gang knew they had a mole in their midst and killed him. The mole's last tip pointed us here. <Col: StageText>Control this area</Col>; we'll be there soon with a team to sweep the area.
stages.dispatch: I put a tracker in those files, so we can trace who's been stealing our armament documents. It definitely was the Tigers, and now they're searching for files. <Col: StageText>Control this area</Col> and neuter those pussies.

stages.owner: A Praetorian informant has discovered some human organs being sold on the black market. We'll intercept them. First step - <Col: StageText>collect</Col> an <Col: StageText>ambulance.</Col>
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians are <Col: StageText>picking up an ambulance</Col> to recover our cache of blackmarket organs. The doc ain't happy. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from mobilizing.

stages.owner: Now you're in possession of the ambulance, go <Col: StageText>pick up</Col> the <Col: StageText>organs</col> so they can't be sold.
stages.dispatch: Praetorian Enforcers are <Col: StageText>seizing </Col> our <Col: StageText>organs</Col>. The doc wants you to <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>. It took him ages to hack them out.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>organs </Col>at this <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>with a cold storage facility. We'll have the forensics team pick them up later and expose the doctor responsible.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians are <Col: StageText>taking</Col> the doc's high value <Col: StageText>organs</col> to be destroyed. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> before they get to where they're going. Unless you want to supply the replacements!

stages.owner: Clean work. Now <Col: StageText>drop off</Col> the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>; it's still city property, you know.
stages.dispatch: This isn't good - the Praetorians are trashing our organ trade. <Col: StageText>Stop them delivering </Col>the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> so they can't use it again.

stages.owner: A second batch of organs has been found but these appear to be animal parts. We've made the traffickers desperate to close a sale. <Col: StageText>Pick up the organs</Col> before they can hit the black market.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians could be on to our whole organ trafficking network. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up our latest shipment</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver these organs</Col> to our lockup. We will destroy them before someone gets a pig's heart sewn inside them.
stages.dispatch: Make or break! The Praetorians could shut down our whole organ trafficking operation with that evidence. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering</Col> it to their warehouse.

stages.owner: A set of organs from a recently escaped orangutan were found in transit. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> the organs before the gang get them to that Crim, Dr. Borious.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> these organs, harvested from an escaped orangutan, before Enforcers can get their hands on them. Dr. Borious will pay good money for this mad scientist shit.

stages.owner: The official Tigers M.D. has confiscated some black market organs he was offered. But you don't want blood all over your ride. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> an <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> first.
stages.dispatch: Some dickhead tried to sell our latest shipment of organs to a doctor who is loyal to the Prentiss Tigers. He is turning the organs in. <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> the Tigers from <Col: StageText>picking up</Col> the transfer <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>.

stages.owner: Nice wheels you got now buddy! The Doc has left the human spare parts out for us to collect. So go <Col: StageText>pick up</Col> the <Col: StageText>organs</col>.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers are on their way to <Col: StageText>confiscate</Col> our shipment of <Col: StageText>organs</Col>. Make sure you <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.

stages.owner: Hey, you got guts. Literally. Ha ha.  <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>organs </Col>at this <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>. Forensics will deal with them there. Don't want them stinking up the place back here.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers have seized our shipment of <Col: StageText>organs</col> and are <Col: StageText>dropping them off </Col>to their forensics team. <Col: StageText>Stop the transfer</Col>.

stages.owner: It's not cool to be seen driving that wreck. Probably smells like a meat counter too. So <Col: StageText>drop off</Col> the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>.
stages.dispatch: That meat wagon has to go. Make sure the <Col: StageText>ambulance </Col>doesn't get <Col: StageText>dropped off </Col>and put back into service.

stages.owner: Gross! Doc uncovered more organs, but they appear to be animal parts. We need to get them before some kid ends up shitting through a baboon's anus. <Col: StageText>Pick up the organs</Col> so we can get rid of them.
stages.dispatch: We had to think fast for our 'budget' transplant patients and get a shipment of animal organs instead. But the Prentiss Tigers are onto us and monkey hearts don't cost peanuts you know!. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>collecting </Col> the organs.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver those organs</Col> to our lockup. We've found a legitimate buyer for them. Just... don't buy any oxtail soup for a while, yeah?
stages.dispatch: The Tigers could halt our trade in animal organs with all the evidence they have. <Col: StageText>Prevent them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering</Col> those monkey tickers.

stages.owner: A set of organs from a recently escaped orangutan were found in transit. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> the organs before the gang get them to that Crim, Dr. Borious.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> these organs, harvested from an escaped orangutan, before Enforcers can get their hands on them. Dr. Borious will pay good money for this mad scientist shit.

stages.owner: The San Paro Standard has been hammering us over the way we do things. Praetorian PR wants you to <Col: StageText>raid these gang premises</Col> and showcase our firm-but-fair community policing.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians are desperately trying to kiss ass with the San Paro Standard by <Col: StageText>raiding our hangouts</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>!

stages.owner: A bust like this will make us look great in the press. <Col: StageText>Take the evidence</Col> from the bust back to the lockup for some 'impromptu' photo opportunities.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians are calling the refuse they recovered  'evidence of positive policing'. WTF? Time to hijack their big press conference. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering</Col> that trash back to their lockup.

stages.owner: Our press release hits and journalists're gonna swarm this place - they'll see it's a shithole! Cover up any tags... Gotta show 'em this place is 100% under our control.
stages.dispatch: 'Torians like to pretend to the press they've wiped us out for a while, by nuking our graffiti. But we pop back like roaches. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>covering our tags</Col>.

stages.owner: Mikko Wong at the San Paro Standard has been saying we only sign up as Enforcers to get laid. <Col: StageText>Raid these gang hideouts </Col>and show her the Tigers can go all the way.
stages.dispatch: The Prentiss Tigers are trying to be tough guys for the cameras. They're <Col: StageText>raiding our hangouts</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.

stages.owner: A bust like this will make us look great. <Col: StageText>Drop off the evidence</Col> from the raid at the lockup. We'll get started on writing the press release.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers grabbed our stuff so they could say their stupid raid was a success to the local press. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering</Col> it back to their lockup. I got a birthday card from my mom in there.

stages.owner: That successful raid is generating some press heat. <Col: StageText>Cover up these tags</Col> to show we're in control of the neighborhood. Hell yeah, we're SO all gettin' laid tonight!
stages.dispatch: Now the Tigers are pretending to be all goody-goody for the camera by wiping off our graffiti. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>covering our tags</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Investigate</Col> this property. Its alarm is linked to a Praetorian security network, and has been going off.
stages.dispatch: We needed to cause a distraction, so I've hacked into the 'Torian security network and I'm setting off random burgular alarms. Help me out. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians</Col> from <Col: StageText>investigating</Col> the alarms.

stages.owner: We've just had another alarm go off. <Col: StageText>Investigate</Col> and try to apprehend the burglar in situ.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians' security network is wide open. I'm setting off more alarms as a distraction. The 'Forcers are running around like headless chickens! <Col: StageText>Don't let them investigate</Col> further.

stages.owner: Another alarm is going off... this can't be a coincidence. <Col: StageText>Force your way inside</Col> and check the place out. Something's going on.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians may be on to the fact I've hacked their network. Buy me time to log out. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>investigating</Col> my set up.

stages.owner: Someone is hacking into the Praetorian system and setting off random alarms, probably to distract us from other crimes. <Col: StageText>Sabotage the antenna</Col> they're using for their uplink.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians have discovered my hacking uplink. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>disabling the antenna</Col> I use to disrupt their systems.

stages.owner: Good work, you've disconnected them from our security system. We've got a fix on the laptop they used to hack the Praetorian server. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the hard drive</Col> from it.
stages.dispatch: They've got a fix on my security alarm hack and tracked down the PC I was using. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>taking the hard drive</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver that hard drive </Col>to the lockup. Once it's analyzed, we should be able to find out who did this and how.  Make sure the criminals don't get their hands on it.
stages.dispatch: The laptop I used to hack the security systems was confiscated by the Praetorians. <Col: StageText>Recover the drive</Col> and return it before they drop it off.
The laptop I used to hack the security systems was confiscated by the Praetorians. <Col: StageText>Recover the drive</Col> and return it before they drop it off.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Investigate</Col> this property. A high number of burglar alarms have been going off in that neighborhood lately.
stages.dispatch: Tigers are giving us grief over in Midtown. I'm creating a distraction here by hacking into alarm systems and setting them off. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating </Col>the alarmed properties and discovering what I'm up to.

stages.owner: We've just had another alarm go off. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>this one and try to catch the burglar red-handed.
stages.dispatch: The security alarm I set off is distracting the Prentiss Tigers. Don't let them find out it's been hacked. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>investigating</Col> the alarms.

stages.owner: The bells, the bells! Another alarm is going off... this can't be a coincidence. <Col: StageText>Force your way inside</Col> and check the place out: something funky is going down.
stages.dispatch: It's fun to watch those Tigers run around chasing their tails. Keep them clueless. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating</Col> the rigged alarms.

stages.owner: Someone is hacking into the alarm systems and setting them off, probably to make sure they keep Tigers off their tail elsewhere. <Col: StageText>Sabotage this antenna </Col>and disconnect them.
stages.dispatch: For a bunch of jocks, those Tigers sure are killjoys. They found out how I've been remotely rigging their security alarms. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>disabling </Col>the uplink <Col: StageText>antenna</Col> I used.

stages.owner: Good work, you've taken the nerds offline. We've tracked the laptop they've been using to hack the alarm systems. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the hard drive</Col> from it.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers disabled all my security alarm distractions and tracked down the hardware I was using. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the hard drive</Col> from the laptop I used for the programming.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver that hard drive </Col>to the lockup. Its cache will tell us who did this and how. Plus, we can see what websites they look at, the dirty bastards.
stages.dispatch: The laptop I used to hack the security systems has been confiscated by the Prentiss Tigers. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering the hard drive</Col> to their lockup and bring it back to me.

The laptop I used to hack the security systems has been confiscated by the Prentiss Tigers. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>delivering the hard drive</Col> to their lockup and bring it back to me.

stages.owner: LaRocha arrested some G-Kings earlier today and found a list of car bomb targets. This is definitely worth further investigation. Check out this vehicle for any explosives, if a bomb is present <Col: StageText>defuse</Col> it.
stages.dispatch: Goddamn Praetorians! LaRocha just stumbled upon our list of city officials targeted for car-bombing. <Col: StageText>Guard the bombs </Col>and make sure no one stops them from going boooom!

stages.owner: The list LaRocha found must be legit. <Col: StageText>Defuse </Col>the <Col: StageText>bombs </Col>from these other vehicles on the target list.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians are trying to defuse the car bombs we've planted around the city. <Col: StageText>Guard the bombs </Col>and make sure no one stops them from going off.

stages.owner: The group behind those car bombs is still looking to cause a major distruption. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>planting more car bombs</Col>.

stages.dispatch: The Praetorians may have defused the bombs we already planted, but we've still got a few new ones left. <Col: StageText>Plant more car bombs</Col> and send the message to the Praetorians that no-one can stop us!

stages.owner: One of the bombers dropped the PDA they've been using to program the bombs. <Col: StageText>Retrieve and hold onto that PDA.</Col>
stages.dispatch: One of our bombers dropped the PDA we've been using to program the bombs. <Col: StageText>Retrieve and hold onto that PDA.</Col>

stages.owner: It looks like the gangs have a vendetta against pro-Derren journalists, and want to cause a news blackout. <Col: StageText>Defuse</Col> any car bombs on this vehicle -  it's top of a hit list we found.
stages.dispatch: We've selected several Enforcer-friendly journalists for a bit of 'censorship' - car bomb style. <Col: StageText>Guard this car </Col>to make sure no one discovers the bomb we've planted in it.

stages.owner: This list must be the real deal. <Col: StageText>Defuse </Col>the <Col: StageText>bombs </Col>from these other vehicles on the hit list we found. They all belong to journalists.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers must have found out about our car bombing plan. <Col: StageText>Guard the bombs </Col>to make sure they go off.

stages.owner: Someone is still looking to drop a cherry bomb down the crapper that is San Paro. Protect the journalists. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>whoever is behind this from <Col: StageText>planting more car bombs</Col>.

stages.dispatch: The Tigers have defused all our car bombs. But there are still plenty of journalists to kill - they breed like San Parian roaches. <Col: StageText>Plant car bombs </Col>in the cars of a sub-editor and his assistant.

stages.owner: One of the bombers dropped the PDA they've been using to program the bombs. <Col: StageText>Retrieve and hold onto that PDA.</Col>
stages.dispatch: One of our bombers dropped the PDA we've been using to program the bombs. <Col: StageText>Retrieve and hold onto that PDA.</Col>

stages.owner: A Praetorian client needs some money transported. <Col: StageText>Pick up the vehicle </Col>they've supplied. Take care of it - you'll need to return it when the job's finished.
stages.dispatch: 'Torians are starting up a new cash delivery service for local businesses. We don't want them running it through our turf. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>getting their vehicle</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the first batch of <Col: StageText>money </Col>our client needs to have transported, and keep it safe.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians will ruin our sources of easy money with their armed escorts. Disrupt their activities. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the cash</Col>.

stages.owner: Now collect the second bag of money our client needs to have transported. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>and keep it safe.
stages.dispatch: It looks like the Praetorians have only sent a small team to protect all that money. This is our chance to do some damage to their reputation. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the cash</Col>.

stages.owner: This is the last collection. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> the <Col: StageText>money </Col>and keep it safe. This is how the Praetorians will take back the city: one job at a time.
stages.dispatch: We don't want all of San Paro's money to be so well guarded. Show the local businesses that hiring armed protection won't do them any good. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>collecting the cash </Col>successfully.

stages.owner: Good work out there. Now <Col: StageText>drop off the cash</Col> and <Col: StageText>return the vehicle</Col> to its owners.
stages.dispatch: Praetorians're spending a lotta time collecting money from local businesses - convenient. <Col: StageText>Stop 'em </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the cash</Col> - we could shut down their whole op in this area.

stages.owner: Great work completing the job, even with those Criminals giving you trouble. <Col: StageText>Stop them robbing </Col>our client's business!

stages.dispatch: Where were you? The 'Torians are gaining an even stronger reputation in this area. Forget the cash. <Col: StageText>Break into this store </Col>and remind everyone who's really in charge.

stages.owner: The Criminals are looking for our client. <Col: StageText>Hold and Protect</Col> his property! Praetorians see that the job's done, all the way to the end.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Capture and Hold</Col> the area. Those toy soldier Praetorians aren't half as tough as they wish they were.

stages.owner: Local business owners are tired of paying protection money to gangs. They've hired the Tigers to protect their weekly cash collection. <Col: StageText>Pick up the vehicle </Col>they've supplied. Don't trash it, dude - it's on loan.
stages.dispatch: Some businesses think we charge too much to 'protect' them from all the nasty gangs around here. They've hired the Tigers to make their weekly cash collection. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from picking up their vehicle.

stages.owner: Head on over to the first collection point. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>money </Col>and keep it safe. And don't scratch the paint job on that loaner too badly.
stages.dispatch: Those business owners are really asking for trouble, calling in those Prentiss brats to protect their cash. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the money</Col>.

stages.owner: No one messes with the Tigers. The next cash drop can be found here. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>money </Col>and keep it safe.
stages.dispatch: If anybody should be getting protection money from the local businesses, it's us. <Col: StageText>Stop the Prentiss Tigers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the money </Col>they're supposed to be transporting safely.

stages.owner: All right! This is the final collection. <Col: StageText>Pick up</Col> the <Col: StageText>money</Col> and keep it safe. With your help, local businesses now see they no longer need to pay gangs for protection.
stages.dispatch: I bet the local businesses are paying the Tigers more for protection than we were charging to leave them alone. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the money</Col> and successfully transporting it.

stages.owner: Nice work. Now <Col: StageText>drop off the cash </Col>and <Col: StageText>return the vehicle </Col>we were loaned. Hope you didn't scratch it.
stages.dispatch: You gotta hand it to the Prentiss Tigers. They're good delivery boys. But <Col: StageText>stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the money </Col>or other businesses might stop paying us protection money too.

stages.owner: Looks like the gangs have turned up to enforce penalties for non-payment. <Col: StageText>Take them out </Col>and <Col: StageText>stop them from robbing </Col>our clients' businesses!

stages.dispatch: We can't have the Tigers ruining our income stream. Get back to basics! <Col: StageText>Break into these stores</Col>. Remind local businesses why they should be paying us to leave them alone.

stages.owner: The Criminals are looking for our the local business owners. <Col: StageText>Hold the area</Col> Tigers are in it to win it, all the way to the end of the game.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Take over the area</Col> Those local business-men have it comin' to them - serve it up, nice and hot.

stages.owner: Most of San Paro's live TV Networks think the Praetorians are corporate and boring. <Col: StageText>Raid this drug factory </Col>and show the press just how exciting our methods can be.
stages.dispatch: What the hell? Every time the Praetorians go looking for news coverage, they pick on us. They're going to <Col: StageText>raid </Col>some of our <Col: StageText>phone hacking dens</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.

stages.owner: Good job! We're getting some good cross-channel coverage after pillaging that drug factory. Now <Col: StageText>raid </Col>this <Col: StageText>drug den.</Col> The use of extreme violence is encouraged.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians really don't encourage you to make a profit in this town. They're going to <Col: StageText>raid </Col>more of our <Col: StageText>phone hacking dens</Col>. Go <Col: StageText>stop them</Col>.

stages.owner: The Networks love what they're seeing. You look awesome in slow-mo! A nearby <Col: StageText>car </Col>was used by the dealers to transport the drugs. <Col: StageText>Retrieve any drugs </Col>it contains.
stages.dispatch: I keep saying: "don't leave the shit in the cars!" So guess what? The Praetorians found a shipment of <Col: StageText>modified SIMs </Col>hidden in one of our courier's vehicles. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from getting to it!

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>drugs </Col>you recovered. This much dope should get convictions for the criminals - and secure us a bunch of prime-time news slots.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians have recovered enough illegal phone numbers to get us all convicted. Unless you want to be implicated, <Col: StageText>stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>dropping those SIMs off</Col>.

stages.owner: Nice job - the Praetorians are headline news. Unfortunately the dealers we pissed off want some prime-time coverage of their own. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>planting bombs</Col> in the area.
stages.dispatch: Our humiliation is all over TV. We could just stay in with a can of Tyler and watch our phone-hacking empire go up in flames, or we could <Col: StageText>blow up</Col> these pissant Praetorian scumbags!

stages.owner: We're onto a middle-class couple who 'keep themselves to themselves' - apart from the multi-million-dollar drug ring they're running out of the family home. <Col: StageText>Raid their drug-packing operation</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers just found $800k in one of our bank accounts. It's from our diamond smuggling operation. Buy us time. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>those Prentiss pussies from <Col: StageText>raiding our accountant's office</Col>.

stages.owner: We busted the husband, but the wife's missing, as are the drug profits. Maybe she's holed up in the other property the couple own. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>their rented <Col: StageText>office</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Shit! The accounts have been frozen, but we can still sell the remaining diamonds. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Tigers <Col: StageText>raiding </Col>our smuggling <Col: StageText>office</Col>.

stages.owner: The Tigers just picked up the wife. She broke down and admitted that she was on her way to get her money laundered. <Col: StageText>Retrieve the dirty cash </Col>from her <Col: StageText>car</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Ah, crap. We got most of the diamonds out the back of the building, but there's one pack left in a courier vehicle. It's always the details! <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the 'Forcers <Col: StageText>retrieving the merchandise</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>money</Col>. The wife transferred most of it to Colombian accounts but you have enough there to convict Mr. & Mrs. 'Nice Neighbors'.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers only have a small sample of our solitaires, but it's enough for a conviction. Stop them <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>the <Col: StageText>diamonds</Col>.

stages.owner: Problem with these supposedly nice, respectable criminals is that they always mix with gnarly-looking dudes. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>planting bombs</Col> in the area.
stages.dispatch: What are we, diamond smugglers or scared newbies? When faced with a crappy jail sentence complete with the Tigers on the other side of the bars, I vote we fight! <Col: StageText>Blow up</Col> the Tigers!

stages.owner: Two Praetorian colleagues were killed in the line of duty. Forensics are at the scene right now. <Col: StageText>Collect </Col>the <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>they've uncovered so far.
stages.dispatch: 'Torians planted drugs on us and then - surprise, surprise - found them. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the drugs </Col>they planted.

stages.owner: Our fallen colleagues were chasing down a gang of criminals. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>money </Col>the cowardly gang dropped as they fled; it could be vital evidence.
stages.dispatch: The cheating Enforcers have gone through several of our homes and taken any savings they can find, saying it's blood money. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up our cash</Col>.

stages.owner: The gang has sprayed up victory <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>gloating about killing our colleagues. <Col: StageText>Cover </Col>it up.
stages.dispatch: These Enforcers clearly don't like it that we have our own territory. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>covering up our graffiti</Col>. Or next time they come back, they'll be trying to evict us.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the damning <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>you have to our <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>. We'll get those murderers yet.
stages.dispatch: Now they have their falsified evidence, the Enforcers are heading back to their plush, cozy offices. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians </Col>from <Col: StageText>making it back </Col>with their sham <Col: StageText>evidence</Col>.

stages.owner: The murdering gang knows you're onto them. The best thing you can do for San Paro is to <Col: StageText>take their territory </Col>away from these Criminals. <
stages.dispatch: We need to make a stand, or the Praetorians will be pushing us around forever. <Col: StageText>Capture this territory and hold it</Col>. This is our turf!

stages.owner: The local gang is trying to expand their domain. They even hired extra graffiti artists to tag more turf up fast. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the deposited <Col: StageText>box </Col>of spray cans so they can't be used.
stages.dispatch: We got some extra guys coming in to help us tag up the area. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up the box </Col>of spray paint we already distributed.

stages.owner: The gang got together a lot of cash to hire some expensive graffiti legends. But no money, no paint. So <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>their <Col: StageText>cash </Col>and we can stop this land grab in its tracks.
stages.dispatch: The graffiti artists we've hired won't work for nothing. We hid their money near where we want the tags. The 'Forcers found it, though. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers taking the cash</Col>.

stages.owner: Good work. It looks like only one of the graffiti posse got through. If you can <Col: StageText>cover up that graffiti </Col>then this is well on its way to being another Tiger triumph.
stages.dispatch: The Prentiss posers aren't just stopping us from tagging the area, they're covering up the work we've already done! <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from <Col: StageText>covering up our graffiti </Col>or we're moving backwards.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Bring </Col>all the <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>you have - the paint and the cash - back to the  <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>and we can build a case against the taggers-for-hire.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers are going back to their hairy lair with our cash and some old paint, presumably to fabricate a court case. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>their <Col: StageText>evidence</Col>.

stages.owner: The local gang didn't appreciate the Tigers halting their expansion. Now it’s 'mano a mano'. <Col: StageText>Stop them taking </Col>back this <Col: StageText>territory</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers want to grab our turf any way they can; maybe one of their daddies wants the real estate! <Col: StageText>Keep our territory</Col> for us.

stages.owner: We have a crazed bomber in lockup, mumbling about angels delivering burning justice to San Paro. Whatever. <Col: StageText>Search his house </Col>and see if you can find some evidence against this nut.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers have arrested our good friend Azrael. Okay, he is a bomb nut seeking to bring about the end of days, but he's still is a good laugh. <Col: StageText>Stop the 'Forcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding his house</Col>.

stages.owner: Inside were incendiary devices and a list suggesting he has already planted some "righteous" <Col: StageText>bombs</Col>. Get to the first location and <Col: StageText>defuse the bomb </Col>while I bring forth a most furious justice.
stages.dispatch: Looks like Azrael was up to his old tricks. <Col: StageText>Guard his bombs </Col>and make sure the 'Forcers don't defuse them. We owe him for his good work in supplying our explosives.

stages.owner: The bomb nut demands to be called Azrael. He has confessed that there are two more <Col: StageText>bombs</Col>. Get to these locations and <Col: StageText>defuse them </Col>before anyone gets hurt.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are really leaning on our buddy Azrael and have discovered his bombing campaign. <Col: StageText>Guard his bombs </Col>and make sure they go off. Whoever Azrael is bombing, they deserve it.

stages.owner: Looks like 'Azrael' has some accomplices who may attempt to bomb these last two locations. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>planting these bombs </Col>.

stages.dispatch: Looks like our friend Azrael was bombing the supporters of a new gun ownership law. <Col: StageText>Plant bombs on the power supply unit </Col>to their campaign HQ and we can finish the job for him.

stages.owner: The bomber has gotten away with this for the last time. <Col:StageText>Take him down</Col>, lethal force is authorized..
stages.dispatch: Bombing sure is fun, but it's time for something a little more personal. <Col:StageText>Take out the Enforcers</Col> that are trying to stop you.

stages.owner: A bookie has gone on the run after being unable to cover his bets. If you offer him protection he'll become one of our star informants. Find him! <Col: StageText>Check out </Col>his business and <Col: StageText>hack </Col>his car's GPS.
stages.dispatch: A bookie owing us money has gone on the run. Make sure the Enforcers don't find him before we do. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating </Col>his business and <Col: StageText>hacking </Col>his car's GPS.

stages.owner: A bookie has gone on the run after being unable to cover his bets. If you offer him protection he'll become one of our star informants. Find him! <Col: StageText>Check out </Col>his business and <Col: StageText>hack </Col>his car's GPS.
stages.dispatch: A bookie owing us money has gone on the run. Make sure the Enforcers don't find him before we do. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating </Col>his business and <Col: StageText>hacking </Col>his car's GPS.

stages.owner: According to the vehicle's GPS data it looks like the bookie's been frequenting this address. It's not on our list of possible hideouts. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>the place and look for signs of the bookie.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers have found clues suggesting the bookie on the run is hiding out here. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding </Col>the place; we need to find him and his money first.

stages.owner: Someone else got to the bookie and took their 'slice' of his profits. <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>weapon </Col>they used. We've got a murder on our hands now.
stages.dispatch: We found the bookie and taught him a lesson. Unfortunately, the 'Forcers found the weapon. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>the forensics that could implicate us.

stages.owner: You've gathered enough evidence for us to move forward with an investigation into who killed the bookie. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>the suspected <Col: StageText>location </Col>of the murder.
stages.dispatch: Our hit guys stashed their bloodstained clothes nearby. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>searching </Col>for this evidence.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>all that <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>back to the lockup. Looks like the bookie has evened the odds in our battle against the Criminals - this will go to court for sure.

stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>all that evidence at our hideout. Without it, the Enforcers have no way of proving who killed the bookie.

stages.owner: Drug dealers are using payphones to keep in contact with their suppliers. Put a <Col: StageText>wiretap on this phone </Col>and we should be able to discover where the dealers are working from.
stages.dispatch: A dealing operation uses payphones to keep in contact with their suppliers. They hired us to <Col: StageText>stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>tapping </Col>their usual <Col: StageText>payphone</Col>.

stages.owner: The dealers are smart enough to not divulge too much information to any one contact. We need more info. The conversations on this other phone may help. Put a <Col: StageText>tap on this payphone </Col>as well.
stages.dispatch: Too late. Enforcers hacked the main phone line to the dealer's suppliers, and are now trying to tap a back-up line. <Col: StageText>Stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>tapping this payphone</Col>.

stages.owner: Great, we put two and two together and got the addresses of a coupla drug dens. Enough listening: time for some action. <Col: StageText>Raid this building</Col> - it's first on the list.
stages.dispatch: Both lines have been tapped. The dealers won't pay us our protection fee now unless we can <Col: StageText>stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding their building</Col>.

stages.owner: That intel was right on the money: drugs are definitely being stored at this location. <Col: StageText>Raid this next building </Col>and <Col: StageText>recover any drugs </Col>found.
stages.dispatch: Having so easily found those stored drugs, our dealer clients are worried the Enforcers will find the location of their other stashes. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>raiding this building</Col>.

stages.owner: Great work. Those phone taps are really gonna keep these dealers in check - until they get wise, that is. <Col: StageText>Deliver the drugs </Col>back to the lockup.
stages.dispatch: Most of the dealer's stashes have been raided and their drugs confiscated. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the drugs </Col>back to their lockup, and we might get our fee out of this yet.

stages.owner: The dealers have no idea how we're on to them and are panicking. They're going to burn any remaining drug stashes. These are in populated areas. <Col: StageText>Stop the arson.</Col>

stages.dispatch: Enforcers found out about the dealer's backup drug stash locations. <Col: StageText>Burn the stash </Col>before the Enforcers are able to confiscate it.

stages.owner: Looks like a safe survived the fire. <Col:StageText>Confiscate</Col> and </Col:StageText>deliver it<\Col> to our lockup.
stages.dispatch: A safe survived the fire! <Col:StageText>Take it to our safe house</Col> and we'll destroy it ourselves.
A safe survived the fire! <Col:StageText>Take it to our safe house</Col> and we'll destroy it ourselves.

stages.owner: We suspect a small group of SPPD officers are working with criminal organizations. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>these recent break-ins where the suspected officers were first on the scene.
stages.dispatch: We have a group of SPPD officers in our pocket, feeding us information and making evidence disappear. <Col: StageText>Stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating </Col>these recent break-ins and uncovering our sources.

stages.owner: We suspect a small group of SPPD officers are working with criminal organizations. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>these recent break-ins where the suspected officers were first on the scene.
stages.dispatch: We have a group of SPPD officers in our pocket, feeding us information and making evidence disappear. <Col: StageText>Stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>investigating </Col>these recent break-ins and uncovering our sources.

stages.owner: The officers' prints and shoe marks are in places that would suggest they committed the break-ins. <Col: StageText>Scan </Col>this <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>to tap into their police radios and download any useful evidence.
stages.dispatch: Enforcers suspect our paid-off cops and are looking for evidence of our having contacted them. <Col: StageText>Stop the 'Forcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>scanning </Col>this <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>to tap into our cell phone records.

stages.owner: The SPPD officers made the calls through one of SPiN's encrypted VOIP services. <Col: StageText>Scan </Col>this <Col: StageText>satellite dish </Col>to access the archived calls.
stages.dispatch: Recordings of our cell phone conversations with the SPPD officers have been found on the telecom company's servers. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>hacking </Col>this <Col: StageText>satellite dish </Col>and downloading them.

stages.owner: The VOIP service still had the calls in their archives - irrefutable proof of the SPPD officers' involvement with Criminals. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>the last known <Col: StageText>locations </Col>of the officers and <Col: StageText>pick up evidence</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The archived calls prove that several SPPD officers are working with us. <Col: StageText>Stop the 'Forcers raiding </Col>the last known <Col: StageText>locations </Col>of the officers until we can get them out of San Paro.

stages.owner: The officers must've felt that someone was closing in on them, and they fled San Paro. <Col: StageText>Drop off </Col>the <Col: StageText>police badges </Col>you found to our <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>. SPPD Internal Affairs can take it from there.
stages.dispatch: Shit! The Enforcers found a cop's badge. It could lead them to our other friends within the SPPD. <Col: StageText>Stop the 'Forcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>dropping off </Col>the <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>they found.

stages.owner: The intel we recovered points to the Criminal staging ground. <Col: StageText>Capture</Col> the <Col: StageText>area</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Those calls must've given the Enforcers enough evidence to lead them to us. <Col: StageText>Defend</Col> our <Col: StageText>block</Col> and don't let them get close.

stages.owner: Our drug enforcement arm need you to take point in an undercover sting operation. It's a San Paro classic: <Col: StageText>pick up this vehicle </Col>and use it to pose as a drug dealer.
stages.dispatch: A plainclothes cop was seen scouting a car nearby. We think the vehicle is going to be used as part of a sting. <Col: StageText>Stop Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up that car</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Drive your vehicle into this area</Col>. Meanwhile, we'll contact some suppliers and see if they'll offer you some drugs to pick up.
stages.dispatch: Enforcers are in an undercover vehicle posing as drug dealers. Now they're cruising round our neighborhood looking for some action. <Col: StageText>Keep them away </Col>from our area.

stages.owner: A supplier has some Angel Ace he stole off his girlfriend... Bad boy. It's stashed it in an alley near your location. <Col: StageText>Pick up the drugs.</Col>
stages.dispatch: A local scuzzball thought the undercover Enforcer was a bonafide dealer, and sold him some Angel Ace. <Col: StageText>Stop the Enforcers</Col> from <Col: StageText>picking up the drugs</Col>.

stages.owner: Okay, we've got some more calls to make. <Col: StageText>Drive your vehicle into this area.</Col> Keep your phone on - the drug pick-up should be close by.
stages.dispatch: Now the Enforcers think our whole neighborhood is full of drug dealers. Their undercover guy is heading into this area to search for a dead-drop. <Col: StageText>Keep them out</Col>.

stages.owner: Next up, a job-lot of 'Nimbus', 'G-Sliders', and 'Goma Tabs'. The drop is in an alley near your location. <Col: StageText>Pick up the drugs</Col>. You play the part of an underworld scuzzbag well... Kinda worries me...
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers have been sold a load of Goma Tabs, to be picked up. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col> from <Col: StageText>retrieving the drugs</Col>. They'll use this an excuse to get heavy in our neighborhood.

stages.owner: Man, this is just like picking candy offa kids. Especially if those kids went to Border High. <Col: StageText>Deliver the vehicle and drugs </Col>back to our lockup.
stages.dispatch: We can reclaim the honor of the neighborhood if we can <Col: StageText>stop the Enforcers </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering the drugs </Col>back to their lockup! They'll use them to stereotype everyone here as a drug addict.

stages.owner: Those suppliers were so happy with you 'pushing so much product' that they want you to make a new pickup of drugs and money. Don't blow your cover: <Col: StageText>retrieve the bag </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>onto it.
stages.dispatch: With all the Enforcer heat in the area, a dealer just bailed and abandoned a bag full of drugs and money. <Col: StageText>Retrieve and hold that bag</Col> - we can't just leave it out there! There are kids in this 'hood.

stages.owner: We're going to do some trick or treating, but last year all we got was hollowpoint. <Col:StageText>Destroy the cameras</Col> to make sure any Enforcers don't spot us and give us a repeat this year.
stages.dispatch: There's an enforcer gang trying to Trick and Treat on our turf! That Candy is ours! We've several cameras in the are to discourage this, so <Col:StageText>Protect the Cameras</Col>.

stages.owner: We're going to do some trick or treating, but last year all we got was hollowpoint. <Col:StageText>Destroy the cameras</Col> to make sure any Enforcers don't spot us and give us a repeat this year.
stages.dispatch: There's an enforcer gang trying to Trick and Treat on our turf! That Candy is ours! We've several cameras in the are to discourage this, so <Col:StageText>Protect the Cameras</Col>.

stages.owner: The cameras spotted us, but we're not stopping.  Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the first <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
stages.dispatch: They got the cameras, but not before they could determine which of the gang is the Trick or Treater! We don't know where he's going, but we have a lock on him. <Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches all his targets.

stages.owner: Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the second <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
stages.dispatch: <Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches all his targets. We've no idea where he's going, so intercept him and take him down.

stages.owner: Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the third <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
stages.dispatch: <Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches all his targets. We've no idea where he's going, so intercept him and take him down.

stages.owner: Escort the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> to the last <Col:StageText>Checkpoint</Col>. The enemy have a bead on the VIP, but they don't know where we're going.
stages.dispatch: <Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> before he reaches the last target. We've no idea where he's going, so intercept him and take him down.

stages.owner: <Col:Opponent_Player>LAST STAGE!</Col>↵The Trick or Treating is Complete! Protect the <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>VIP</Col> and <Col:StageText>Kill the Enforcers</Col> so we can go retire to gorge on candy.
stages.dispatch: <Col:Opponent_Player>LAST STAGE!</Col>↵The VIP has completed his Trick of Treating! <Col:StageText>Kill the VIP</Col> but make sure to <Col:Target_VIP_Friend>Stay Alive</Col>.

stages.owner: A contact of Tyron's paid him with counterfeit bills, and you've been picked to be our avenging angels. <Col: StageText>Rob </Col>the contact's <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and take back the goods we sold him.
stages.dispatch: A recent spate of burglaries by the Blood Roses has local businesses running scared. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from would-be burglars.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>Tyron's recovered <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>nearby. Lucky for the contact, we can't find him; crossing the Roses is the last thing you ever do... just ask Darryl Kent's dead girlfriend.
stages.dispatch: Blood Roses have managed to get away with some goods. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the <Col: StageText>loot </Col>from being taken to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The contact has two more <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>nearby. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>them too, and take the *real* cash the contact should've paid us with in the first place.
stages.dispatch: More local businesses are now at risk from the Blood Roses. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from them and ensure that the burglars don't get away with anything. Particularly money.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to the same <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>that you took the loot to. Tyron says he's already set up another deal for the goods you recovered; looks like we've come up smelling of roses as usual.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses are hauling ass with the money they just stole from those businesses. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the Roses from getting that <Col: StageText>cash</Col> to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Seems the contact might have made a deal for protection after ripping us off. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>all <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>in the area.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses think that they've gotten away with this - we need to show them otherwise. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>all <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>in the area.

stages.owner: Know the shit we steal in our skate-bys? A fence we use to move it has been paying us with fake bills! I never did like that greasy-haired cockbag. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>his <Col: StageText>dens </Col>and reclaim our goods.
stages.dispatch: A recent spate of burglaries by the G-Kings has local businesses running scared. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from would-be burglars.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>our recovered <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>nearby. I'll start hooking us up with someone more worthy of the G's trust.
stages.dispatch: G-Kings have managed to get away with some goods. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the <Col: StageText>loot </Col>from reaching the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The fence has two more <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>nearby. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>them and take the cash the fucker should've paid us in the first place.
stages.dispatch: Now those G-Kings are all fired up, more local businesss are likely to be at risk. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from them and ensure that the burglars don't get away with any cash or goods.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to the same <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>that you took the loot to. This is the Gresty way; double or nothing. If you rip someone off then you better get ready to hold on to your shit.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings are making a run for it with the money stolen from those businesses. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>from reaching this <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Seems the fence might have made a deal for protection after ripping us off. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>any and all <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>who show up in the area.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings think that they've gotten away with this - we need to show them otherwise. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>all <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>in the area.

stages.owner: We had tags up in this area for a while, marking this as Blood Rose turf, but some highly un-chic locals cleaned them off and installed security cameras.<Col: StageText> Destroy those cameras </Col>so we can bring sexy back.
stages.dispatch: A couple of local blocks are under threat from those rich-bitch Blood Roses. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>cameras </Col>we installed to protect the neighborhood from their Nu-Bushido bullshit.

stages.owner: Excellent. With those cameras neutralized, we can re-claim this block for the Roses. Now go <Col: StageText>spray </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>as a statement of our intent to colonize.
stages.dispatch: Those arrogant Blood Rose snobs think they can just waltz into this neighborhood and spray their graffiti. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations</Col>; we'll make them pay for every incursion.

stages.owner: Good job; now <Col: StageText>destroy </Col>some more <Col: StageText>cameras </Col>nearby and we can claim that block, too. You're handling yourself with a certain amount of style, so far. Good to see.
stages.dispatch: Damn, with that last block lost, it's twice as important that we hold this one. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>cameras </Col>so we can coordinate a counter-attack. Street by street, we'll take San Paro back...

stages.owner: Toss up and maintain two more<Col: StageText> tags </Col>for a little while, and you're done. You're eager to please... Wouldn't make that too obvious to Charlotte; you'll end up recruiting in Breakwater Marina, wearing too little leather.
stages.dispatch: Damn, those Roses are hard to kill. They're planning to tag this block too. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and keep their Ravanelle-wearin' asses out of this neighborhood.

stages.owner: We had tags up in this area for a while, marking this as skater turf, but some locals cleaned 'em off and installed security cameras. <Col: StageText>Destroy </Col>those <Col: StageText>cameras </Col>so we can re-write our tags.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings are threatening some security cams we put up to deter their graffiti. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>those <Col: StageText>cameras </Col>before the damn skater-punks destroy them.

stages.owner: Nice work. With those cameras nuked, this turf'll be ours again. <Col: StageText>Tag up </Col>these <Col: StageText>walls </Col>and make sure they stay tagged - let the locals know they live in G-Town now!
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings think they can just waltz into a decent, law-abiding neighborhood and spray their graffiti. Big mistake. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations</Col>; show them that street resistance is alive and well.

stages.owner: You can handle yourself; here's another area for you. <Col: StageText>Destroy these cameras </Col>and we'll claim that block too. Watch your back: this time they're ready for you, G.
stages.dispatch: Damn, with that block lost we need to hold the next. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>cameras </Col>and protect the neighborhood from those jumped-up Gresty board rats.

stages.owner: Rock. OK, <Col: StageText>spray </Col>up a last few<Col: StageText> tags</Col> and <Col: StageText>make sure Enforcers don't spray over them</Col>. Maybe a design inspired by Shift's latest: Mayor Derren trying to skateboard, arms flailing and skirt flying up.
stages.dispatch: This is it. The G-King tag team is out to claim this final block:<Col: StageText> protect</Col> these <Col: StageText>walls </Col>from their bad art - they have some new design showing Mayor Derren trying to skateboard, and it's... undignified.

stages.owner: A senior politician needs a liver transplant: too many champagne lunches on the taxpayer's dime, it seems. We plan to hold that liver to ransom.<Col: StageText> Hack </Col>this<Col: StageText> antenna </Col>to access the ambulance comms.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses have taken to hijacking organs on their way to and from hospitals, for sale on the black market. <Col: StageText>Protect</Col> this <Col: StageText>antenna</Col> from Byron's hackers, or they'll be able to tap into ambulance radio chatter.

stages.owner: We found an ambulance near you. Head there and <Col: StageText>steal</Col> the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>. They won't hand over the liver unless you look the part; you'll have to ditch the custom wheels and drive - ugh - a plain EMS van.
stages.dispatch: An ambulance has been misdirected into Blood Rose territory and is now at risk. <Col: StageText>Defend</Col> this <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> and ensure that it isn't stolen for use in their organ-trafficking racket.

stages.owner: The donor liver was recovered from a morgue. <Col: StageText>Head over there</Col> with the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> and make the pick-up. He'd be waiting forever for a match without the Roses - this politician will owe us.
stages.dispatch: With that ambulance stolen, looks like the Blood Roses are on their way to meet a black market contact. <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col>; don't let it reach the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver</Col> the <Col: StageText>liver</Col> and bring the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We've already made the call - we get that politician his liver, and Simeone gets a friend in government.
stages.dispatch: Damn, it looks like the Roses got those organs - and with this city's E.R.s full of gunshot victims in need of transplants, they'll clean up! <Col: StageText>Intercept</Col> the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> and <Col: StageText>organs</Col> before they reach the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.dispatch: There's a bag full of cash nearby - it must be the payment for the Roses' trouble. <Col: StageText>Recover</Col> the <Col: StageText>bag</Col> and <Col: StageText>keep</Col> it away from them - those rich kids hate having their toys taken away.

stages.owner: All right - <Col: StageText>deliver</Col> the <Col: StageText>liver</Col> and bring the <Col: StageText>ambulance</Col> back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We've already made the call - we get that politician his liver, and we get a friend to the Benjamins in government.
