stages.dispatch: Nearby is what must be the payment for the G-Kings' trouble. <Col: StageText>Recover the bag of cash</Col> and <Col: StageText>keep </Col>it away from them. Maybe they'll realize there are easier ways to earn money.

missions.title: LOOK AT ME, LOOK AT ME

stages.owner: Michael Simeone has a meeting with some big international buyers at the airport. He has asked us to ensure that 'Forcer attention is elsewhere. <Col: StageText>Set fire </Col>to this <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses have been seen filling up the gas tank of a nearby car. That always means arson. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>, to show we're clamping down on wanton destruction.

stages.owner: Good start, but we need more, so <Col: StageText>burn </Col>these <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>. Michael's meeting is going well, but there are a lot of stolen items to trade, thanks to you kleptomaniacs.
stages.dispatch: More vehicles are under threat of arson. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>, and I'll put extra teams on patrol at gas stations so this won't escalate.

stages.owner: Michael reports that both Praetorians and Prentiss Tigers are closing in on his meeting. Time to orchestrate a serious decoy. <Col: StageText>Burn these buildings </Col>to the ground.
stages.dispatch: Good news: the car burning has stopped. Bad news: the Blood Roses have moved on to burning buildings. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from these pyromaniacs.

stages.owner: Looks like that got the attention of our valiant Enforcers. Keep them busy by shooting them in the face till they give up! <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>for the next 5 minutes, until Michael signs the deal.
stages.dispatch: Looks like we flushed the Roses out and have them on the run. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>all of the <Col: StageText>arsonists</Col> - they can go burn in hell instead.

stages.owner: We used to get a lot of money for protecting this neighborhood, but now everyone's complacent. <Col: StageText>Set fire </Col>to this <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>: it's in a prime spot to scare the locals.
stages.dispatch: Local citizens are under threat from arsonists: <Col: StageText>protect </Col>the targeted <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and show the populace that we can keep the city safe.

stages.owner: Further intimidation is needed to stop the locals thinking that was a one-off. <Col: StageText>Set fire </Col>to these other <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>, too. Burn to earn.
stages.dispatch: More vehicles are under threat of arson. Must be attempted intimidation by the G-Kings. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>and it'll demonstrate the worth of Enforcement.

stages.owner: That kinda worked... the locals sought out protection - from Enforcers rather than G-Kings! We need to make this more personal. <Col: StageText>Set fire </Col>to some of the resident's <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The recent G-King arson attacks were designed to intimidate the local citizens into paying for protection. Their next target is these nearby <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>; show everyone what <Col: StageText>protection </Col>really means.

stages.owner: Looks like the 'Forcers have been called in. Go <Col:StageText>fill 'em full of holes</Col>.
stages.dispatch: We can't go around firefighting the problem like this - literally. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>G-King arsonists </Col>once and for all.

stages.owner: A chopshop owner hasn't paid for vehicles that your fellow Blood Roses stole for him. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>the first <Col: StageText>car </Col>we stole for him; maybe that will scare him into compensating us.
stages.dispatch: One of our undercover operatives posed as a chopshop owner to entrap the Blood Roses, but they may be onto him. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>one of his <Col: StageText>cars </Col>from being <Col: StageText>bombed</Col>: it's prime evidence.

stages.owner: No remuneration yet from our friend Mr. Chopshop. The second stolen <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>is nearby. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>that one too. And I'll send him an email saying that we'll keep blowing cars up - until he coughs up.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses are trying to destroy a chopshop owner's <Col: StageText>van </Col>nearby. They must know he is one of our moles. <Col: StageText>Protect it </Col>and draw the Roses out into the open.

stages.owner: Our chopshop friend is about to sell a sweet <Col: StageText>car. </Col>Go and <Col: StageText>bomb</Col> it before his customer gets there. If we hurt his income he should change his wallet-shy behavior.
stages.dispatch: We are trying to gather photographic evidence of Blood Roses attempting to bomb cars. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>car </Col>until we can get into place with our telephoto lens.

stages.owner: Instead of paying us what's owed, the chopshop owner replied to my email with 'Screw you, Blood Poseurs'. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>this <Col: StageText>shop </Col>he uses as a front: let's make this personal.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses have outsmarted us. They must know it's a set-up and have now targeted our other fronts in this area. Change of tactic: <Col: StageText>protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>shop </Col>from the bombers.

stages.owner: We need to wipe out all of this guy's businesses or no one will take the Roses seriously in San Paro again. Another team has planted some explosives on his electronics shop. <Col: StageText>Protect the Explosives</Col> from the bomb squad.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses could expose our whole undercover operation. They seem to know exactly which shops our people own. <Col: StageText>Defuse our Property</Col>.

stages.owner: We need to wipe out all of this guy's businesses or no one will take the Roses seriously in San Paro again. Another team has planted some explosives on his electronics shop. <Col: StageText>Protect the Explosives</Col> from the bomb squad.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses could expose our whole undercover operation. They seem to know exactly which shops our people own. <Col: StageText>Defuse our Property</Col>.

stages.owner: The chopshop owner has called in some expert armed help. For the cost of all this, he coulda just paid us in the first place. <Col: StageText>Eliminate everyone </Col>he has hired.
stages.dispatch: Enough is enough. We need to <Col: StageText>take out </Col>this group of <Col: StageText>Blood Roses </Col> before our whole undercover operation is blown wide open.

stages.owner: The names of the jury in a pending case against the G-Kings has been leaked. Arlon Benjamin wants us to make sure they vote the right way. <Col: StageText>Plant a car bomb </Col>under the <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col> of the head juror.
stages.dispatch: A big trial against the G-Kings is about to get under way, and they have a reputation for leaning on jury members. <Col: StageText>Protect the car </Col>of the head juror from car bomb attacks.

stages.owner: This second jury member is a gardener, apparently. <Col: StageText>Plant the bomb in his van</Col>. Geddit? Plant? I crack myself up sometimes.
stages.dispatch: A second <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>is nearby, belonging to another witness. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the vehicle from the G-King bombers.

stages.owner: The law says you should be judged by your peers, but no one is as awesome as the G-Kings. So <Col: StageText>plant the car bomb </Col>under this juror's car and he can feel the awesomeness for himself.
stages.dispatch: If you don't stop these car bombs, the G-Kings on trial will be aquitted. This <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>, belonging to a jury member,  will probably be the next target. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>it.

stages.owner: Who lives in San Paro and doesn't own wheels? This loser juror, apparently - but the G-Kings are equal opportunity bombers. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>her <Col: StageText>shop </Col>and we'll have one more vote of 'not guilty'.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings have changed tactic and targeted the workplace of a jury member. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>shop </Col>from the bombers. We must give every citizen the confidence to stand up against thugs.

stages.owner: One of the jury members dropped out; you intimidated well, my friend. We've planted a bomb at the store of his replacement. <Col: StageText>Protect the bomb</Col> from the authorities.
stages.dispatch: Well done; the big trial is going ahead as planned. But the G-Kings have changed tactic to focus on the star witness instead. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb</Col> that has been set at his place of work.

stages.owner: One of the jury members dropped out; you intimidated well, my friend. We've planted a bomb at the store of his replacement.<Col: StageText>Protect the bomb </Col> from the authorities.
stages.dispatch: Well done; the big trial is going ahead as planned. But the G-Kings have changed tactic to focus on the star witness instead. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb</Col> that has been set at his place of work

stages.owner: Your campaign of friendly influencing has drawn attention - big time. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>the incoming <Col: StageText>opposition</Col> - or the jury will feel free to vote anyway they see fit. Can't have that.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings are set on intimidating everyone involved in this trial. San Paro must have faith in its Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>and defeat any <Col: StageText>G-Kings </Col>involved in perverting the course of justice.

missions.title: IN, OUT, SPRAY IT ALL ABOUT

stages.owner: A city street-cleaner removed all our graffiti from the nearby block. Other gangs may try to take this territory. <Col: StageText>Spray </Col>our tags back onto the <Col: StageText>walls </Col>and keep it G-King.
stages.dispatch: The graffiti removal team has been in and cleaned off all the G-King filth. But the Gs are stubborn and stupid enough to come back to reapply their tags. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>from being sprayed.

stages.owner: Are you on a sightseeing trip or something? Pick up the pace. Get over to our territory and <Col: StageText>tag these two spots, </Col>before some local bad boys take a shine to it. Don't let anyone try and mess with your work.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the G-Kings from respraying their tags on to these two <Col: StageText>locations</Col>. I don't go around putting graffiti on *their* stuff. Well... one time I did.

stages.owner: It's starting to look a bit more G around here again. Broken-in, like wearing your favorite leather knife sheath. <Col: StageText>Spray </Col>these last couple of <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and don't let anyone beat you to it.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the last couple of <Col: StageText>locations </Col>from the G-King graffiti crew who want to claim this area.

stages.owner: Job done - now muzzle your nozzle and <Col: StageText>lock and load</Col>. A graffiti removal team is headed your way - <Col: StageText>take them out</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Washing off graffiti isn't the answer: it just comes back. We need to wash the G-King scum themselves into the sewer. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>G-King taggers</Col>.

stages.owner: The Tigers have been an annoyance lately, interfering with our contracts. We need to slow them down, and luckily we've got a plan. Start by <Col: StageText>raiding </Col>these minor dealers' <Col: StageText>drug dens</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses seem to be 'rehearsing' for Hell Night; we've had reports of Blood Rose crime all over San Paro. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>Blood Rose <Col: StageText>raids </Col>on these local <Col: StageText>properties</Col>.

stages.owner: Excellent. Those drugs are going to appear in Orlenz's possession soon. For that trick to happen, you need to <Col: StageText>steal </Col>his <Col: StageText>car</Col>. He's visiting Tigers in the area, so it should be easy to find.
stages.dispatch: Jeung usually only lets his Roses off the leash once a year, but he must be feeling generous today. Lucky us. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>from Blood Roses out to steal it.

stages.owner: Good, good. Now <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the car and <Col: StageText>drugs </Col>to the stage we've set. Will this setup get that smarmy asshole Orlenz' convicted? I doubt it, but it'll cause the Tigers some trauma at least.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Rose revelers are escaping with <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them. These Hell Night events can rival the CSA riots for mass looting. Thank heck this isn't the actual Hell Night...

stages.owner: An "anonymous tip" would make them suspect the Blood Roses straight away. <Col: StageText>Hack </Col>this <Col: StageText>antenna, </Col>and we'll use the Tiger radio network to send false reports guiding them to the drugs instead.
stages.dispatch: The Roses have worked themselves up into a frenzy with all the other crimes they've committed, and now they're targeting our property as well. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>our <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>from the Blood Rose revelers.

stages.owner: Our play is set, but you've left a loose end. Some people spotted you with the car. You need to <Col: StageText>kill the witnesses, </Col>or our little plan won't work. You do want the plan to work... don't you?
stages.dispatch: Trying to stop these Hell Night 'rehearsal' crimes is getting us nowhere. Time to treat the disease rather than the symptoms: <Col: StageText>take out </Col>the <Col: StageText>Blood Roses</Col>. They can't cause trouble if they're dead.

stages.owner: Some of my compañeros got hooked on Fade, and now they just sit around spaced out and doing fuck-all. It's boring, so I want to help them kick the habit. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>their <Col: StageText>houses </Col>and steal the Fade.
stages.dispatch: A rookie of ours made the mistake of trying to hit on Double-B. We're still finding pieces of him. His unit retaliated, and now we've got a war on our hands. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the G's <Col: StageText>attacks </Col>on our <Col: StageText>homes</Col>.

stages.owner: I know Monkeywrench hides Fade in his ride. He's out cold at the moment, so just <Col: StageText>steal </Col>his <Col: StageText>car </Col>for now. I'll get it back to him later, so don't fuck the car up too much - or you're paying for it.
stages.dispatch: This little war that's broken out between us and the G-Kings is worse than usual. Getting too close to home for me, even. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>my <Col: StageText>car</Col>: those bastards are eyeing it.

stages.owner: Cool. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the car and <Col: StageText>drugs </Col>over here. I'll get our Gs to clean the car out and dump the Fade. Sucks to do this, but those asshole friends of mine will thank me for it later.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings are a pain to deal with at the best of times; if only that rookie hadn't stirred up the hive. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>G-King looters from bringing the <Col: StageText>loot and my car </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: I want to make sure my compañeros don't get heat for this - <Col: StageText>hack </Col>this <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>so I can check Enforcer chatter and make sure it's all cool. If they don't ID Monkeywrench's car then we're good.
stages.dispatch: They've gotten away with people's goods, and my car - and now they're screwing with our equipment! <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>our <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>from those G-Kings.

stages.owner: Fuck! There's Praetorians on their way. Did you get spotted with the car? <Col: StageText>Kill the Enforcers </Col>so they can't interfere. I'll have to hook Monkeywrench up with new license plates now.
stages.dispatch: Ok, enough is enough. <Col: StageText>Take out </Col>the <Col: StageText>G-Kings</Col>. They really need to emphasize those 'do not fraternize with the enemy' lessons in our training. Anything to avoid another G-King incident like this.

stages.owner: A local loser is going to testify against us in court. He saw us trying to attach a tug to the Mist restaurant and tow it down the canal. <Col: StageText>Torch </Col>his <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>to make him change his story.
stages.dispatch: The Mist floating restaurant called us in to provide protection. A gang got busted trying to tow it down the canal with a tug boat and are now intimating witnesses. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this witness's <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>.

stages.owner: I guess people don't like it when you try to tow away the floating restaurant they're eating in. <Col: StageText>Burn </Col>the customers' <Col: StageText>cars </Col>to help them 'forget' the whole thing ever happened.
stages.dispatch: Who would be dumb enough to try to steal a whole floating restaurant - with people in it? These maniacs need to face their day in court. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>of the witnesses.

stages.owner: It would have been so cool to have our own floating restaurant. Shame they moored it so tightly. <Col: StageText>Burn </Col>these <Col: StageText>properties </Col>belonging to the owner and she may drop the charges against us.
stages.dispatch: This gang would be dangerous if they weren't so dumb. <Col: StageText>Protect these buildings </Col>that belong to the Mist restaurant's owner. The gang don't want her to testify in court against them.

stages.owner: The Mist restaurant has called in some bounty hunters. Looks like they want to see us either in court - or dead. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>the <Col: StageText>bounty hunters </Col>and try to <Col: StageText>stay alive</Col>. They'll get bored eventually.
stages.dispatch: This gang are a cucumber short of a salad, you know what I mean? <Col: StageText>Eliminate the gang</Col>. You'll be doing us all a favor by removing them from the gene pool.

stages.owner: An unknown group did a series of drive-bys on our friends. <Col: StageText>Bomb </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>they used. This doesn't seem to be the work of the usual local gangs.
stages.dispatch: I love watching San Paro's Big Talent. Now the contestants who got voted off are on the hunt for revenge. <Col: StageText>Protect the car </Col>of the show's winner from being bombed by this gang of losers.

stages.owner: The second vehicle used in the drive-by against our fellow members is nearby. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and get some payback. I'll look into who these drive-by dickwads are.
stages.dispatch: A second car is nearby, belonging to one of the Big Talent TV show judges. <Col: StageText>Protect the car </Col>from the 'The Bombastics'. If they wanted to do even more damage they'd sing instead.

stages.owner: These drive-by nuts are planning an even bigger attack. They have started to weld gun mounts onto the inside of a car. <Col: StageText>Bomb the vehicle </Col>so it can never be used against us.
stages.dispatch: These losers have a lot of anger, maybe if they'd put this much energy into their band they wouldn't have been voted off San Paro's Big Talent. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the TV exec's <Col: StageText>car </Col>from their bombs.

stages.owner: These drive-by dickwads are legitimate businessmen just killing for kicks. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>their <Col: StageText>store </Col>and see how they like it when we come and mess with their business.
stages.dispatch: These tuneless wonders have upped their game, unlike their talent. Now they're targeting the sponsors of the Big Talent show as revenge for being booted off. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>stores</Col>.

stages.owner: These guys don't even need the money! <Col: StageText>Protect the bomb</Col> we've planted at the other store that belongs to these part-time gangsters. They bring a whole new meaning to the term 'white collar crime'.
stages.dispatch: This group of talentless singers really hold a grudge. They are attacking the sponsor of their main rival. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb</Col> that's been placed at the sponsor's property.

stages.owner: These guys don't even need the money! <Col: StageText>Protect the bomb</Col> we've planted at the other store that belongs to these part-time gangsters. They bring a whole new meaning to the term 'white collar crime'.
stages.dispatch: This group of talentless singers really hold a grudge. They are attacking the sponsor of their main rival. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb</Col> that's been placed at the sponsor's property.

stages.owner: Looks like these 'hobby hoods' fancy a real fight. <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>off the part-time <Col: StageText>gangsters </Col>and humiliate them into never messing with real Criminals again.
stages.dispatch: We can't let these bunch of talentless singers go around causing wanton destruction. If they want to sing - it should be like a jailbird. <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>and defeat the <Col: StageText>group</Col>.

stages.owner: You know how Al Capone eventually got caught, income tax evasion. We could eliminate other gangs in the same way, by bombing their accounts. <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>bomb <Col: StageText>components </Col>from this <Col: StageText>building</Col>.
stages.dispatch: A small, specialist gang of bombers has arrived in the area. This could be bad news. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>from any attempt to break in, it contains bomb casings.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>more bomb <Col: StageText>components </Col>from this <Col: StageText>building</Col>. We need it to be extra incendiary to make sure the accounting paperwork catches fire.
stages.dispatch: These bombers mean business, they plan to steal some ultra high density ballistics. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>where it's kept.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>the specialist <Col: StageText>bomb fuse </Col>from this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and we'll have everything we need to destroy the other gang's accounts. Who says accounting is boring?
stages.dispatch: The bomb makers are hitting another <Col: StageText>building </Col>- get there and <Col: StageText>defend </Col>it. It contains the fuses they'd need. No news on the bomb target yet.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Take </Col>all of the bomb <Col: StageText>components </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>so they can be assembled. I wonder if we can claim them on expenses - they are work related.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the bombers <Col: StageText>taking </Col>their <Col: StageText>components </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. They have everything they need to build some serious ordinance.

stages.owner: Head to the <Col: StageText>building </Col>where some of the gang store their accounts and plant the <Col: StageText>bomb </Col>to blow it up.
stages.dispatch: The bombers are on their way to blow up our bomb squad offices. The squad itself has been called out on a job so you'll have to <Col: StageText>defend the building </Col>from attack.

stages.owner: The other gang know we've hit them hard and they don't like it. <Col: StageText>Wipe out </Col>any <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>who remain in the area and we can take their territory. I'm sure Al Capone would approve.
stages.dispatch: With our bomb squad temporarily out of action the bombers will be a powerful force in the area. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>bombers </Col>and halt their reign of terror before it starts.

stages.owner: An economic downturn means our revenue is dropping. We had to slash the prices of all our goods and now we need more. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and grab some new stock.
stages.dispatch: The economic downturn has made the Criminals ever more desperate, they need to steal even more goods to sell. <Col: StageText>Defend these properties </Col>from being burgled.

stages.owner: WTF? Mink driving gloves? Okay, no biggie. We'll still shift 'em. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the stolen <Col: StageText>goods </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>those stolen <Col: StageText>goods </Col>before they reach the burglars' <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Times are tough for everyone out there - why should the gangs get a free ride?

stages.owner: It turns out that the customers who would normally buy those mink driving gloves are staying home right now. <Col: StageText>Break into this <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and steal something for home entertaining.
stages.dispatch: More civilian properties are under attack from local burglars. <Col: StageText>Defend this building </Col>from them, the Criminals seem to be picking out only high value items.

stages.owner: Okay, I didn't actually mean a box of gold plated sex toys, but whatever. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the stolen <Col: StageText>goods </Col>to our specialist <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>location.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>goods </Col>before those burglars get them to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. They must be planning something big with all the profit from this job.

stages.owner: A snitch has informed us of a rare guitar that's been spotted across town. <Col:StageText>Capture the item</Col> before the enforcers do, it should be worth a lot.
stages.dispatch: The burglars are planning on stealing a rare guitar. Get to it first and <Col:StageText>retreive the instrument</Col> to keep it out of criminal hands.

stages.owner: Art's also a commodity and a piece has turned up nearby. <Col: StageText>Race to </Col>this second <Col: StageText>item</Col> and <Col: StageText>claim it</Col>. I've been told it's an original 'Shift' print.
stages.dispatch: There's a piece of art nearby that the burglars are targeting. <Col: StageText>Race to </Col>the painting and <Col: StageText>claim it</Col>.

stages.owner: High-End Electronics sell for a fuck-ton. <Col: StageText>Get to </Col>this third <Col: StageText>item </Col>and <Col: StageText>claim it </Col>before your opponents do.
stages.dispatch: They're going for electronics now. <Col: StageText>Race </Col>the burglars to the <Col: StageText>gear </Col>and <Col: StageText>claim it </Col>for the people of San Paro.

stages.owner: There's a back-alley hospital that have foolishly left some organs unguarded. <Col: StageText>Race to </Col>the penultimate <Col: StageText>items</Col> and grab them before anyone else does. They'll sell for a fortune.
stages.dispatch: Shit, they've found an organ donor facility. <Col: StageText>Race </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and <Col: StageText>claim the organs</Col>.

stages.owner: Screw this legal shit, there's a stash of drugs at the next place. <Col: StageText>Get to </Col>the <Col: StageText>drugs</Col> and <Col: StageText>claim them </Col>too.
stages.dispatch: Last one: The criminals have found a stash of narcotics that were hidden by a rival gang. Get there before them and <Col: StageText>grab</Col> the drugs before the crims get their hands on them.

stages.owner: Ok, collect the items and <Col:StageText>drop off the majority</Col> at our shop to sell.  We should make a lot of money off this lot.
stages.dispatch: Ok, now <Col:StageText>grab the items</Col> and <Col>drop them off</Col> at our facility. You'll need at least 3 of them.

stages.dispatch: Ok, now <Col:StageText>grab the items</Col> and <Col>drop them off</Col> at our facility. You'll need at least 3 of them.

stages.owner: We've offered a generous protection deal to the locals, but not everyone has seen sense. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and take a few things - just to highlight the value of our proposition.
stages.dispatch: We've been asked to help protect this neighborhood. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>. They're getting broken into on a regular basis.

stages.owner: That's good, hopefully they'll see the value of our insurance policies. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. May as well sell it and get some cash.
stages.dispatch: Burglars stole cash from several buildings that fall under our jurisdiction. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the <Col: StageText>stolen property </Col>from ever <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>the Criminals' <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Two local businesses have consistently ignored our messages - so we need a bigger, more personal, persuasive gesture. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>their <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and steal any cash or stock that you can carry.
stages.dispatch: Those burglars are getting cocky, hitting the businesses of a couple of our major clients. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and ensure that nothing is stolen.

stages.owner: Nicely done. The business owners probably expected the Enforcers to protect them, but this is our city, not theirs. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>stock </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The burglars managed to grab two large <Col: StageText>bags </Col>of cash and stock from those businesses. If you can <Col: StageText>stop </Col>them <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>we can save face with our client.

stages.owner: Our protection racket has proven lucrative and now everyone wants in on the action. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>to hold onto this neighborhood. Protect the protection racket.
stages.dispatch: The burglars have threatened our income and our reputation. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and prove that the Enforcers won't tolerate criminal behavior.

stages.owner: The Enforcers have been planning to hold a local fun day to draw in new recruits and win over the brain-dead citizens. Use <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>to mark up this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and remind where the local power lies.
stages.dispatch: We have a community open day planned for this area. As usual, the gangs want to spoil it. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>from the gang's graffiti artists.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Tag </Col>some more <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and then <Col: StageText>hold </Col>them; make sure that the locals know who's in charge around here. Clue; it ain't the 'Forcers.
stages.dispatch: Graffiti artists are also targeting these <Col: StageText>locations</Col>. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>those locations and keep this neighborhood clean and safe for our forthcoming community open day.

stages.owner: Let the Enforcers have their stupid cutesy family fun day, just so long as our graffiti looms over it. <Col: StageText>Tag </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and then <Col: StageText>hold </Col>them.
stages.dispatch: The local gangs are keen to make their presence known during our community open day. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these last <Col: StageText>locations </Col>from their ugly graffiti. Let's keep things clean.

stages.owner: You done the tagging, now comes the fragging. You've not be invited to the family fun day it seems. <Col: StageText>Take out </Col>these disrespectful <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>and make it clear that you don't need an invite.
stages.dispatch: You just know the gangs are going to ruin our community event if they get a chance. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>gang </Col>members, or the mofos will be back to burn down the coconut shy.

stages.owner: Our fence, Wes, is in the market for the Onset CDX-G1: an expensive media center car stereo with all the bells and whistles. Head to this <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and <Col: StageText>loot </Col>it: we're pretty sure it's got one.
stages.dispatch: The new multimedia car stereo from Onset is on sale today. It's already sold out, so everyone's after them. Our spotters saw thieves casing a nearby vehicle for the stereo. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>car</Col>.

stages.owner: Take the stolen Onset <Col: StageText> car stereo </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>point for Wes to collect. Those things cost a fortune, and they're rare as hell. Should net us a pretty penny.
stages.dispatch: Thieves took an Onset CDX-G1! <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them taking the stolen <Col: StageText>stereo </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. People go crazy for anything these days... I once saw a woman stab someone over the last Kiki doll in the store.

stages.owner: A couple of our spotters hit the streets and found some more Onset stereos. <Col: StageText>Loot </Col>these <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>and get those Onset CDX-G1s - Wes is offering us a good price for them.
stages.dispatch: A patrol identified two more vehicles being cased by thieves. <Col: StageText>Guard </Col>the <Col: StageText>cars </Col>. Those thieves're trying to make a quick buck off desperate consumers willing to buy stolen Onset stereos.

stages.owner: Nice, a couple more Onset stereos - take the <Col: StageText>stereos </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>. Y'know Wes is our fence, but did you know his name is actually Wesley D. Fence? Talk about being born to do a job.
stages.dispatch: The thieves got what they were after. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the stolen <Col: StageText>stereos </Col>reaching the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Some cities have to deal with riots over hunger or human rights... In San Paro? Car stereos. Seriously.

stages.owner: Wes left our <Col: StageText>payment here</Col>. <Col: StageText>Recover</Col> it and <Col: StageText>keep it</Col> away from our enemies.
stages.dispatch: We need to recover those stolen Onset stereos. Some are hidden nearby: <Col: StageText>take </Col>and then <Col: StageText>keep </Col>the <Col: StageText>bag </Col>containing the stereos away from the thieves, and any crazed consumers.

stages.owner: You heard of the Goody Gundrops? Yeah? Well, we've got collectors willing to pay for the latest Gundrops figurines. We spotted people buying some from a shop: <Col: StageText>loot </Col>their <Col: StageText>cars </Col>for the models.
stages.dispatch: New Goody Gundrops merchandise has hit the streets. They're so popular that we had a full-blown riot last time - so be careful. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>cars </Col>of those buying Gundrops merchandise.

stages.owner: Ok, <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the first of those <Col: StageText>figure packs </Col>to this collector's <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Funny how popular the Gundrops are with all ages; a friend of mine has a Peppermint Pistol handbag.
stages.dispatch: Rabid Gundrops fans have stolen figurines. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>figure packs </Col>before they can be hidden at the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. I promised my cousin a Peppermint Pistol doll... hope there's some left.

stages.owner: Our second <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>isn't far from you. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the second <Col: StageText>figure pack </Col>there. This collector wants the Maple Magnum figure - good choice!
stages.dispatch: The fans are taking stolen Gundrops figurines to another <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>figure packs</Col>. Think this is bad? You missed the fight that broke out over a Strawberry Shotgun pencil case.

stages.owner: Ok, last one! Hurry and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>figure pack </Col>to the final collector's <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. That pack has Cookie Cannon and Raspberry Rifle in it, right? Whatever. They've already paid us, either way.
stages.dispatch: There's only one <Col: StageText>figure pack </Col>left! The Gundrops looters are taking it to a <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them. Hey - is that a Cookie Cannon pack they've got? That's my niece's favorite Gundrops character!

stages.owner: Shit. It seems we've attracted some attention: you've got desperate Gundrops fans after you. They must think you've still got the models. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>some <Col: StageText>fans </Col>to scare off the rest.
stages.dispatch: There're people everywhere after Gundrops items; we need to bring things under control. <Col: StageText>Take out </Col>any <Col: StageText>looters </Col>you find. ...If you find a Peppermint Pistol doll, I'll - ahem - take it into custody.

stages.dispatch: A local gang is trying to disable our security and fire systems so they can attack our property. Three <Col: StageText>transformers </Col>control the power to this entire area. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the first one from saboteurs.

stages.owner: The second power <Col: StageText>transformer </Col>is nearby. <Col: StageText>Sabotage </Col>this one as well. Once we've disabled all three transformers the alarm systems in the buildings we targeted will go offline.
stages.dispatch: The second <Col: StageText>transformer </Col>is under attack from a local gang. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>it from any attempt at sabotage - if all three transformers are disabled our properties will be vulnerable.

stages.owner: One power <Col: StageText>transformer </Col>remains. <Col: StageText>Sabotage </Col>this one and the alarms on our target buildings will be deactivated, clearing the way for our attack.
stages.dispatch: One <Col: StageText>transformer</Col> remains. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>it from sabotage or our security and fire systems will be de-activated and the Criminals will attack our properties.

stages.owner: The alarms are down and the targets are vulnerable - <Col: StageText>destroy these buildings </Col>by setting them alight. This business is about to learn that the only reliable security is OUR security.
stages.dispatch: With the power down our alarms and sprinklers have been shut off - <Col: StageText>defend </Col>our <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from the attacking arsonists.

stages.owner: Now we just need to drive the message home - <Col: StageText>wipe out </Col>any <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>who remain in the area. Make sure ALL the local businesses know their high-tech security don't mean shit.
stages.dispatch: Damn, they destroyed our buildings! We can't let this attack go unpunished. <Col: StageText>Wipe out </Col>any <Col: StageText>arsonists </Col>who remain in the area.

stages.owner: All right. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>that <Col: StageText>safe </Col>back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. It doesn't look like the Enforcers have opened it yet, so the WP execs will still be able transfer their money out of those 'ghost' accounts.
stages.dispatch: Our case against those Wilk-Pastor execs rests on the accounts held in that <Col: StageText>safe</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Criminals before they can get the safe to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: As agreed, an exec from Wilk-Pastor left our payment of unmarked bills in a <Col: StageText>briefcase</Col>. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the case and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from any Enforcers who get in your way.
stages.dispatch: Wilk-Pastor left payment for the Criminals in a <Col: StageText>briefcase</Col>. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>that case and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>it away from the Criminals. It may be the last chance we get to link the WP execs to the gang.

stages.owner: The Enforcers seem whiter-than-white, but their allies are anything but: Valentine Foods have used toxic additives in their products for years to cut costs. <Col: StageText>Sabotage </Col>the <Col: StageText>power </Col>to their security.

stages.owner: Those photos are enough for the media to question who the Enforcers are really protecting: the people or the companies. For now though, <Col: StageText>burn </Col>those <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>to keep them out of circulation.
stages.dispatch: The spies have what they need, but they must have gotten instructions to destroy our client's existing stock of ingredients. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these <Col: StageText>supplies </Col>from arson attacks.

stages.owner: Almost done. Now just <Col: StageText>burn </Col>the second batch of those 'Bio Snacker' <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>to stop them reaching the public. Don't worry, I'm sure that the smoke is harmless... just, y'know. Try not to inhale any.
stages.dispatch: There's only one <Col: StageText>pallet </Col>of Mr. Clock Corn Chip additives left, so we need to <Col: StageText>defend </Col>it from the spies. Don't let them destroy our client's stockpile.

stages.owner: We've embarrassed the Enforcers, so now they need a high-profile success. That means you. They're coming after your group leader - <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>all <Col: StageText>opposition </Col>and <Col: StageText>ensure </Col>your <Col: StageText>group leader survives</Col>.
stages.dispatch: To stop those corporate spies, we need to target their ringleader. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>their <Col: StageText>group leader </Col> and they'll think twice before attacking companies we're protecting again. <Col: StageText>Avoid taking casualties</Col>.

stages.owner: We hired a crew from out of town to hit an armored car for us, but they've kept the haul for themselves. <Col: StageText>Get the gold back from </Col>their <Col: StageText>hideouts </Col>- it's rightfully ours!
stages.dispatch: We heard that Criminals are planning a large-scale burglary of several local pawnbrokers all at once. These <Col: StageText>buildings</Col> are the most likely targets. <Col: StageText>Defend</Col> them from the burglars.

stages.owner: Ain't that shiny. I can almost understand why they'd betray us... Almost. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>gold </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals managed to steal a lot of <Col: StageText>gold</Col> from under our noses. Unless you wanna be a laughingstock on N3's evening show, <Col: StageText>stop</Col> the Criminals before they get to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The bulk of the haul is still with the leaders of the crew we hired. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>their <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and <Col: StageText>take </Col>the <Col: StageText>loot </Col>.
stages.dispatch: The perps are targeting more <Col: StageText>buildings</Col> - guess they think our heads are up our asses! <Col: StageText>Defend</Col> those targets and <Col: StageText>retreive</Col> any of the <Col: StageText>loot</Col> they manage to take.

stages.owner: If I don't get those safes back you can kiss your asses goodbye. <Col:StageText>Drop them off</Col> at the safe house and <Col:StageText>stop the Enforcers</Col> retreiving them.
stages.dispatch: Get those safes back and <Col:StageText>Drop them off</Col> at our safehouse. Stop the Criminals from capturing them.

stages.owner: A snitch is under 24-hour 'Forcer protection. A little chaos might lure his guards away: we're thinkin' hardcore porn, on three electronic billboards around the city. <Col: StageText>Hack this sat dish </Col>to start with.
stages.dispatch: Heads up. Something's going on. Suddenly we got Crim crews headed to almost every <Col: StageText>satellite dish </Col>in San Paro, all at once. I smell trouble. You're detailed to <Col: StageText>protect </Col>this one; get going.

stages.owner: Heh heh. Fender-benders galore... <Col: StageText>Hack this satellite </Col>to get us access to the second billboard. Another broadcast of raunchy porn oughtta draw the Enforcer protection away from that snitch's van.
stages.dispatch: Another Crim crew on the move. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>satellite dish </Col>from them; it belongs to an advertising company that does electronic billboards. We got rookies trolling Lie-Net for clues...

stages.owner: That snitch has intel on us in his van. From all the honking and laughing I can hear, our porn-billboard distraction is pretty effective. <Col: StageText>Hack one more dish </Col>to tie traffic right the fuck up.
stages.dispatch: Shit on toast. The hacked billboards are broadcasting hardcore porn at major intersections, causing all sorts of fender-benders and shit. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>dish </Col>nearby or it'll get even worse.

stages.owner: We're gonna make that snitch regret that betraying us even crossed his fuckin' mind. He hid his intel in bombproof cases somewhere in his van - let's test their craftsmanship. <Col: StageText>Blow up the van</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Looks like some sort of anti-corporate thing - all the hacked billboards were run by the same business. Lie-Net suggests Crims might target the company's courier <Col: StageText>van </Col>- <Col: StageText>protect </Col>it.

stages.owner: There's a fuck-ton of intel in those cases; that snitch must've been planning to rat us out for months. <Col: StageText>Get the cases to our drop </Col>before Enforcers can retrieve them.
stages.dispatch: That van contained sensitive marketing plans and private information, kept in secure cases. We need to <Col: StageText>get the cases here </Col>before the Crims get away with them.

We're going to attack that network but we need <Col: StageText>hardware</Col>. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>everything to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: We need more computers for our denial-of-service attack on the Enforcer Dispatch.Net. Luckily, a shipment of TOSHIO server machines that we can use is being transported. <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>that server <Col: StageText>van</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Those hackers are trying to establish a network and are after even more hardware. We anticipate an attack on this <Col: StageText>van </Col>full of TOSHIO computers. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>it from any attempted theft.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>computers </Col>in the back of that van to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Try and get 'em there in one piece; bullet holes tend to cause a drop in hardware performance.
stages.dispatch: The "Zero Override" hackers stole a van full of TOSHIO <Col: StageText>computers </Col>and now they're headed to this <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>those computers before the geek collective can put them to use.

stages.owner: We'll need to boost our signal for the DoS attack, and that takes a lot of power. First, <Col: StageText>sabotage </Col>this <Col: StageText>electrical box </Col>and fix it up to serve our needs.
stages.dispatch: The hackers plan to use those PCs to attack vulnerable networks throughout the city, harvesting them for any personal data they can sell. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>junction box </Col>and stop them patching in.

stages.owner: All right, that oughtta be enough power. Now <Col: StageText>hack </Col>this <Col: StageText>transmitter </Col>and we'll jack their network. I've got guys all over the city waiting to start crazy heists once the network is down.
stages.dispatch: The "Zero Override" hackers are after a number of vulnerable wireless networks with valuable personal data, and they plan to boost their signal using this <Col: StageText>satellite</Col>. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>that target.

stages.owner: The Enforcement Dispatch.Net has slowed to a crawl. They'll try to shut us down, so we need to hold this location. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>the <Col: StageText>checkpoint </Col>.
stages.dispatch: "Zero Override" may have established their network, but we're going to move in and shut them down. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>the area while we move into position.

stages.owner: One of the starlets from the latest copy of Effigy has been somewhat... indiscreet, and we've been hired to clean up after her. First <Col: StageText>recover</Col> the <Col: StageText>drugs</Col> she left in this <Col: StageText>car</Col>.
stages.dispatch: We have a couple of kilos of narcotics from a recent raid, which could help put some Blood Roses behind bars. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>our <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and see that looters don't take our evidence.

stages.owner: There are several photographs of the pop starlet doing something that definitely wouldn't fit with her "angelic" persona. <Col: StageText>Steal</Col> the photos from the photographer's <Col: StageText>studio</Col>.
stages.dispatch: A DVD of surveillance footage from an anti-narcotics sting operation is in this building, but Blood Roses have been sniffing around. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>from Blood Rose burglars.

stages.owner: Now we need you to bring in the <Col: StageText>drugs</Col> and the <Col: StageText>photos</Col> and try to prevent another San Paro scandal. <Col: StageText>Deliver</Col> everything to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Damn, we need to get that <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>back. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>it from being delivered to the Blood Rose <Col: StageText>hideout</Col>.

stages.owner: All right, now we're going to <Col: StageText>burn</Col> the <Col: StageText>office</Col> of the reporter who's been poking his nose into other people's business.
stages.dispatch: Our base of operations for the recent investigation was a building nearby. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>from arsonists sent by the Blood Roses to destroy our case notes.

stages.owner: All right, the starlet's agent has left us our payment as agreed. <Col: StageText>Take</Col> the <Col: StageText>money</Col> and <Col: StageText>keep</Col> it safe from any opposition.
stages.dispatch: Shit, there's only one chance left. We need to recover the proceeds from the recent drug dealing. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>that <Col: StageText>money </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep </Col>it from any opposition.

stages.owner: A friend of our very own Princess Bonita has been somewhat... indiscreet, and we're on clean-up duty for her. First <Col: StageText>recover</Col> the <Col: StageText>drugs</Col> which she left in this <Col: StageText>car</Col>.
stages.dispatch: We have a couple of kilos of narcotics from a recent raid which could help put some G-Kings behind bars. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>our <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and see that the G-Kings don't take our evidence.

stages.owner: There are also several compromising photos of Bonita's good friend on her night out. <Col: StageText>Steal</Col> the photos from the paparazzo's <Col: StageText>office</Col>.
stages.dispatch: A DVD of surveillance footage from the anti-narcotics sting operation is in this building, but G-Kings have been sniffing around. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>from burglars.

stages.dispatch: Damn, we need to get that <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>back. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>it from being delivered to the G-King <Col: StageText>lockup</Col>.

stages.owner: Hmmm... looks like the Paparazzo made copies, so we're going to have to <Col: StageText>burn</Col> the <Col: StageText>office</Col> of the reporter he sent them to. Make sure there's nothing left but cinders.
stages.dispatch: Our base of operations for the recent investigation was a building nearby. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>from arsonists out to destroy our case notes.

stages.owner: All right, Bonita has left us a little payment for our good deeds. <Col: StageText>Take</Col> the <Col: StageText>money</Col> and <Col: StageText>keep</Col> it safe from any opposition.
stages.dispatch: Shit, there's only one chance left. We need to recover the proceeds from the recent drug dealing. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>that <Col: StageText>money </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep </Col>it from any opposition.

stages.owner: A drug dealer has been peddling his shit on our turf, and it's affecting Blood Rose recruitment. <Col: StageText>Burgle</Col> these <Col: StageText>buildings</Col> and get hold of as much of his stash as you can.
stages.dispatch: Thieves hired by the Blood Roses have been scoping out some properties nearby. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and ensure that none are burgled.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver</Col> all of those <Col: StageText>drugs</Col> to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> and we'll leave an "anonymous" tip for the Enforcers. They can deal with that fool AND his stash.
stages.dispatch: It seems like we've stumbled into a drug war. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the <Col: StageText>drugs </Col>from being delivered to the Blood Roses' <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Fucking Enforcers got the wrong idea, they seem to think that shit belongs to us. Oh well - <Col: StageText>kill</Col> your <Col: StageText>opponents</Col>, before they can put you down.
stages.dispatch: We can't let those dealers get that shit into circulation. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>all <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>in the area. We'll send in the narcotics boys later to clean up the mess.

stages.dispatch: G-King thieves have been scoping out some properties nearby. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and ensure that none are burgled.

stages.owner: The Enforcers hired a specialist IT company to hack into our emails. Not hard; half of us still have 'bloodrose' as our password. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the IT <Col: StageText>offices </Col>and steal their network hard drive.
stages.dispatch: We've hacked into the Blood Rose email system and are downloading all their messages. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the PC and hard drive in our <Col: StageText>offices</Col>. The Roses are bound to try and steal it.

stages.owner: Good work. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>hard drive </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> and we'll ensure that it's dealt with delicately. With a giant, ladylike magnet.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses knew exactly what they were after, and they've taken the <Col: StageText>hard drive</Col>. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>it before it reaches their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Shit. The Enforcers made copies of all the emails. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and recover the DVD back ups. If you see anyone, CC: them with a bullet from me.
stages.dispatch: Luckily we backed up all that data onto disk. But the Blood Roses must know that too. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from being broken into by the Roses. We've got the disks stored there.

stages.owner: Excellent. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>disks </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>so Byron can examine them - he might be able to trace how they hacked us.
stages.dispatch: Damn, we really can't afford to lose that data. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>disks </Col>before they are delivered to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The Enforcers are shifting from a cyber attack to a real attack. <Col:StageText>Kill the Enforcers <\Col> and <Col: StageText>Survive </Col>long enough for us to wipe these disks and patch our network security issue.
stages.dispatch: This is too high tech for me. Who wants to read their spam, anyway? <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>all <Col: StageText>Blood Roses </Col>in the area. Click 'Delete' on their asses.

stages.owner: The G-King online poker room is going great, mainly 'cause it's fixed. 'Forcers have been monitoring it, though, and downloading all the stats. <Col: StageText>Burgle this building </Col>and take their hard drive.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings have been running an online poker site called 'Royal Kings'. We hacked their server and found the games are rigged. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>our IT <Col: StageText>office </Col>while we download the incriminating data.

stages.owner: Pocket aces, G. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>hard drive </Col>to this <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we can get back to fleecing Neo1984 and his buddies out of their cash.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings knew exactly what they were after, and they've taken the <Col: StageText>hard drive </Col>out of our machine. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and wipe it.

stages.owner: The Enforcers have raised the stakes. They made disk back-ups of the G-King poker site stats. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and recover the disks.
stages.dispatch: We have an offsite disk back-up of all incriminating data. The G-Kings must know this. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from being burgled, that's where the disks are stored.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>disks </Col>to this <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>so that we can give them a G-King royal flush! Nice.
stages.dispatch: Damn, without that data we won't be able to shut down the G-King's rigged poker site. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them and our <Col: StageText>back-up disks </Col>before they're delivered to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: I guess 'Forcers don't like cards. Their poker face is for shit, and they ain't bluffing. Show them we've got an ace up our sleeve by <Col: StageText>giving them the bullets</Col>.
stages.dispatch: I bet the G-Kings rigged this game too. Not that I'm sore loser, but can you go and <Col: StageText>eliminate</Col> all the <Col: StageText>G-Kings </Col>in the area? Rockin'.

stages.owner: Devereaux made a new line of jewelry in honor of her latest conquest. The conquest's husband isn't pleased. Out of sympathy (a.k.a., he paid), we've agreed to <Col: StageText>bomb stores </Col>selling the jewels.
stages.dispatch: Our client, Devereaux, released a line of jewelry dedicated to her newest lover. The line is being targeted by the lover's unhappy husband. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>stores </Col>selling the jewels from bombing attacks.

stages.owner: Good thing we dig the jilted husband's cause (he paid us well), 'cause you just blew up a lot of valuable shit. <Col: StageText>Bomb </Col>this <Col: StageText>storehouse </Col>containing the remaining jewels to finish the job.
stages.dispatch: With the jewelry stores in ashes, the jilted husband's thugs are targeting the remaining jewels Devereaux is keeping in this storehouse. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>storehouse</Col>.

stages.owner: Good work! Now,<Col: StageText>kill</Col> any 'Forcers your bombs attracted. I don’t know about revenge being sweet, but it sure as hell pays well.
stages.dispatch: Those bombers destroyed a half a city block just to get back at Devereaux. We can't let them get away! Find the <Col: StageText>bombers</Col>, and <Col: StageText>eliminate </Col>them.

stages.owner: Select players have got early copies of the new Battle Kaiser IV game. It's so popular that people will pay big money for it. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>these <Col: StageText>properties </Col>and steal the advance copies.
stages.dispatch: The Battle Kaiser tournament champions have received preview copies of Super Battle Kaiser IV. Desperate gamers plan to steal those copies, so <Col: StageText>protect </Col>the champions' <Col: StageText>properties</Col> from burglary.

stages.owner: All right! Bring those <Col: StageText>advance copies </Col>of Battle Kaiser to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We'll sell two - and keep one for ourselves; some of our crew play that series at tournaments.
stages.dispatch: Those gamers ran off with the Super Battle Kaiser IV preview copies. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>delivery of the <Col: StageText>stolen games </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Battle Kaiser III was ok, but fans are hyped for the new stuff in Super.

stages.owner: Rabid Battle Kaiser fans have agreed to pay us an extortionate amount for those two advance copies. They've left the <Col: StageText>money </Col>nearby - <Col: StageText>pick it up </Col>and keep it away from anyone trying to take it.
stages.dispatch: It looks like some major money changed hands over those Super Battle Kaiser IV preview copies. The dead drop for the <Col: StageText>payment </Col>is nearby - <Col: StageText>grab </Col>it and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>out of the thieves' hands.

stages.owner: That asshole Judas Goldwright is back and trading weapons again. Guy lives up to his name: last time we used him, he sold us out. Judas's got weapons in these <Col: StageText>lockups</Col>. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>them and take the whole shebang.
stages.dispatch: An arms dealer, Judas Goldwright, has been working with us to take down the larger Criminal organizations. Another arms dealer, Harmony, is interfering. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>Judas's <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>.

stages.owner: Nice haul; mostly Somatic and Agrotech small arms. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>handguns </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>, but don't get too relaxed. Judas lured us into an Enforcer trap before, so he could be up to something.
stages.dispatch: Thieves sent by Harmony have stolen Judas's <Col: StageText>ammo </Col>supplies. They're taking 'em to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the thieves before they get there. Judas needs the ammo to convince our target to meet him.

stages.owner: Judas sold rifles around here for a while. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>this <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>and search for the stash. Watch for ambushes. Ever since Judas crossed us, we've stuck to Jericho for hardware.
stages.dispatch: Judas has a large stash in another <Col: StageText>building</Col>. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>it from Harmony's men. Without the weapons, Judas has no chance of luring our target to the meeting we plan to ambush.

stages.owner: A whole bag full of rifles - this seems too easy, but I won't look a gift horse in the mouth. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>bag </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. This'll stock up our weapon arsenal nicely 'til the next drop.
stages.dispatch: Harmony's men are escaping with a <Col: StageText>bag </Col>containing weapons. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them before they get to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. It's bait for our ambush, and Harmony having more arms to sell isn't in our best interests.

stages.owner: Fuck, I knew Judas would have something set up. The bag of rifles had a tracking chip sewn into the lining. Enforcers are headed this way. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>points </Col>to hold off the strike team.
stages.dispatch: Shit, Judas is a genius. Even without the weapons Harmony stole, he managed to lure our targets to a meeting. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>points </Col>to prevent our targets escaping the ambush. We've got 'em now!

stages.owner: A CSA scrub-crew went round and took down our colors. We've repainted some of the walls with their blood, but you better go fix our <Col: StageText>tags </Col>before anyone gets the idea this place is up for grabs.
stages.dispatch: Blood Roses and G-Kings have been embroiled in a turf war, with us fighting it out in the middle. A patrol spotted a G-King crew <Col: StageText>tagging </Col>up the area with their colors. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them.

stages.owner: Cool. <Col: StageText>Tag </Col>the next area those CSA assholes scrubbed clean. They took days stripping off that paint, and now it's about to be tagged up again... ahh, the fickle joys of territory control.
stages.dispatch: That graffiti crew has moved on to tag another location - <Col: StageText>defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>area</Col>. We might be fighting a war on two fronts, but we can't let them just do whatever they feel like.

stages.owner: One more should do - toss up a <Col: StageText>tag </Col>to mark this turf as ours. Hopefully the Enforcers will get the message this time; as much as I love putting them in body bags, it's not like ammo is free.
stages.dispatch: Now Gs are <Col: StageText>tagging </Col>this area - <Col: StageText>stop </Col>them putting up gang colors. While I'd love to see the G-Kings and Blood Roses wipe each other out, the civilian casualties from the fights aren't worth it.

stages.owner: Looks like our example wasn't enough: there's another cleaning crew headed your way. <Col: StageText>capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>them, so we can finish putting up tags.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Rose/G-King battle is headed your way - <Col: StageText>capture </Col>these key <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and keep Crims out of the area. We need to make a stand to minimize the number of civilians caught in the crossfire.

stages.owner: The campaign to re-elect Councillor Davis is gaining ground - too much ground. You need to get some dirt on this pro-CSA candidate. <Col: StageText>Disable </Col>the <Col: StageText>power </Col>to her campaign offices. The power is split between 3 boxes; this is the first.
stages.dispatch: Criminals don't want to see Councillor Davis re-elected, and her campaign offices could come under attack. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>electrical box </Col>which provides power to the office security systems.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Disable </Col>the second of three <Col: StageText>electrical boxes </Col>- once the power is fully down you can break into the 'Re-elect Davis' campaign headquarters undetected. ↵
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the next <Col: StageText>electrical box</Col> - if the system is powered down, the security on Councillor Davis' campaign offices will be exposed. She's a major Enforcement cheerleader.

stages.owner: One more <Col: StageText>electrical box </Col>should do it. <Col: StageText>Disable </Col>it and the power will finally go down. Then we can see what the Councillor Davis campaigners don't want the public to know.
stages.dispatch: The power will fail if another <Col: StageText>electrical box </Col>is disabled. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>it from the attackers. With no power Councillor Davis' campaign offices will be open to attack.

stages.owner: Excellent. The power will stay down for 5 minutes. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the three <Col: StageText>offices </Col>used by the committee to re-elect Councillor Davis. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>whatever you find.
stages.dispatch: The power will be down for 5 minutes so it's up to us: <Col: StageText>protect </Col>the political campaign <Col: StageText>offices </Col>from the burglars. It's like the Watergate break-in all over again.

stages.owner: Excellent. The power will stay down for 5 minutes. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the three <Col: StageText>offices </Col>used by the committee to re-elect Councillor Davis. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>whatever you find.
stages.dispatch: The power will be down for 5 minutes so it's up to us: <Col: StageText>protect </Col>the political campaign <Col: StageText>offices </Col>from the burglars. It's like the Watergate break-in all over again.

stages.owner: What a find! An undeclared slush fund. I think maybe I should go into politics. I have most of the skills already! <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The burglars have stolen money donated by honest citizens who want to see an end to Criminals in San Paro. <Col: StageText>Stop the gang </Col>from <Col: StageText>delivering </Col>it to their <Col: StageText>hideout</Col>.

stages.owner: Councillor Davis' supporters aren't content to fight just at the ballot box, they are on the streets and after you. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>your <Col: StageText>opponents</Col>. Politics is a dirty game after all.
stages.dispatch: Those security systems have failed, the political system has failed - but we won't fail. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>your <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>and show them a little democracy in action.

stages.owner: We've been hired by Tastyburger for a bit of corporate espionage. Break into this <Col: StageText>car </Col>and <Col: StageText>steal </Col>a product sample from Noodle Shack.
stages.dispatch: Noodle Shack have hired us for some professional corporate protection during their product launch. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>car </Col>belonging to the head of sales. An exclusive new product is inside.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>that stolen fast food <Col: StageText>sample </Col>to a safe <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>location. The guys from Tastyburger will be along to collect it later.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the <Col: StageText>delivery </Col>of the stolen Noodle Shack <Col: StageText>food sample </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>location. We promised it would be safe under our protection.

stages.owner: The Tastyburger execs are worried about their competitor's new menu item. It tastes great. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>the <Col: StageText>car </Col>of the CEO and <Col: StageText>steal </Col>the <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>there that contains the secret recipe.
stages.dispatch: Keep security tight on this. Noodle Shack are paranoid that someone will steal their new secret recipe. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the CEO's <Col: StageText>car </Col>while he's in a meeting.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the stolen <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>location. The Tastyburger bosses will pay a lot for Noodle Shack's secret recipe.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Prevent delivery </Col>of the stolen <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>containing the Noodle Shack secret recipe. If it reaches the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>location, we'll lose them as clients.

stages.owner: Looks like Noodle Shack have hired in their own team of ninjas! <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>off any <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>who are foolish enough to try and eliminate you.
stages.dispatch: Corporate protection provides the income that funds our work. <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>off any <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>hired by Tastyburger and we can make this a good pay day.

stages.owner: One of our members has betrayed us and joined a rival gang. We're going to frame him and get him put away. First you'll need to <Col: StageText>steal </Col>his <Col: StageText>car</Col>, then we'll have fun with it - in his name!
stages.dispatch: Car thieves are targeting a lowrider parked in the area. <Col: StageText>Protect the car </Col>from the thieves.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the traitor's <Col: StageText>car </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location </Col>- and don't worry about the people of San Paro seeing it. In fact - the more, the merrier!
stages.dispatch: The gang are taking the stolen car to a nearby <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>car </Col>before it arrives. It may contain clues.

stages.owner: A few more witnesses will help to further incriminate the traitor. <Col: StageText>Drive </Col>his <Col: StageText>car </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location</Col>. It's all part of the show.
stages.dispatch: The gang is trying to lose us - they're taking the <Col: StageText>lowrider </Col>to another <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>before they arrive.

stages.owner: This is how we treat traitors. <Col: StageText>Bring </Col>his <Col: StageText>car </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and we'll make sure that there are no prints on it - apart from his, of course.
stages.dispatch: An informant just called in: those guys are planning to heist a distillery warehouse. Think that's the getaway vehicle? <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>car </Col>before it arrives at the new <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: OK - now for the good part. <Col: StageText>Burn </Col>these two <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>. The traitor's car being so close will place him at the scene. Genius.
stages.dispatch: Shit! That gang's gotta know we're onto their distillery job - they're setting fire to other vehicles to try and keep us busy. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>those <Col: StageText>cars</Col>!

stages.owner: Great, break out the marshmallows. <Col: StageText>Torch </Col>these nearby <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>. When our traitorous friend is blamed for these arsons, he'll be put away for years.
stages.dispatch: This gang are getting out of hand. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings</Col> - we can't allow civilians to be drawn into the crossfire.

stages.owner: A few people witnessed your recent activity and could link us to those fires, instead of the traitor. <Col: StageText>Wipe out </Col>any <Col: StageText>witnesses</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The distillery is locked down, but we need to bring order to this situation right now!  <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>Criminals </Col>before anyone else gets hurt!

stages.owner: For years, Wex Corp has been donating funds to the Derren administration. We're going to dig up some dirt and discredit the company. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>the director's <Col: StageText>car </Col>and take anything juicy.
stages.dispatch: Mayor Derren's administration has been generously funded by Wex Corp for years, but Criminals are planning to shut down the company using corporate espionage. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the MD's <Col: StageText>car </Col>from attack.

stages.owner: That PDA is a start, but we're gonna need something more incriminating than the fact that the MD of Wex Corp has Tastyburger on speed dial! <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the CEO's <Col: StageText>office </Col>and take any data you find.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals are moving on to a Wex Corp fabrication centre. They’re planning to burgle it and sell product information to the company's commercial rivals. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>from burglars.

stages.owner: Hmmm... the CEO ain't stupid enough to keep the incriminating stuff at his office. Try his <Col: StageText>place</Col>. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the building and grab any useful information, then <Col: StageText>deliver everything </Col>back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Those burglars have valuable product data from the Wex Corp offices. Now they're heading towards the CEO's home. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>and <Col: StageText>intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>data </Col>before it reaches this <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Hmmm... the CEO ain't stupid enough to keep the incriminating stuff at his office. Try his <Col: StageText>place</Col>. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the building and grab any useful information, then <Col: StageText>deliver everything </Col>back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Those burglars have valuable product data from the Wex Corp offices. Now they're heading towards the CEO's home. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>and <Col: StageText>intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>data </Col>before it reaches this <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The data on that PC looks interesting - the CEO visits 'San Paro Ho Cam' a lot! We're more interested in the encrypted files, however. <Col: StageText>Guard </Col>the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>for <Col: StageText>5 minutes </Col>while we decrypt them.

stages.dispatch: The Criminals are analyzing the sensitive R&D data they stole from Wex Corp's CEO - we have about <Col: StageText>5 minutes</Col>to <Col: StageText>capture </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and recover that data before they can crack it.

stages.owner: Those files were eco impact reports: ground water contamination, fish stock depletion, rats with more heads than a football team... Good stuff. <Col: StageText>Return </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and <Col: StageText>collect </Col>the <Col: StageText>PC</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals have collected all the manufacturing secrets they gained from Wex Corp and put it on a PC ready for delivery to foreign buyers. <Col: StageText>Stop the gang </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the <Col: StageText>hard drive</Col>.

stages.owner: The San Paro Standard is gonna be real interested in the data you found regarding Wex Corp's toxic dumping record. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>PC </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from our enemies.

stages.dispatch: We have to <Col: StageText>recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>PC </Col>containing Wex Corps' commercial data. <Col: StageText>Deliver it </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from the corporate thieves.

stages.owner: Lindochem are putting experimental "anti-aggression" chemicals into our neighborhood water supply. Makes me wanna kill someone! <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>their <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and take the <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Criminals have been paid to steal a new "anti-aging" formula that Lindochem spent millions developing. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and <Col: StageText>stop </Col>any stolen <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>reaching the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Lindochem are putting experimental "anti-aggression" chemicals into our neighborhood water supply. Makes me wanna kill someone! <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>their <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and take the <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: I'm not sure what's in that formula, but my nipples are tender and my piss is blue. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these Lindochem <Col: StageText>offices </Col>and take any relevant <Col: StageText>documents </Col>you find to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> ASAP.
stages.dispatch: Criminals have a sample of the anti-aging formula, but now they're after Lindochem's research notes. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and <Col: StageText>stop </Col>any <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>reaching the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
