stages.owner: We sold that information to the San Paro Standard - soon everyone's going to know about Lindochem's chemical experiments! <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>our <Col: StageText>payment </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold it </Col>so Lindochem's gang-for-hire doesn't get it.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals were paid in cash for the anti-aging research they've stolen. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>payment </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from the gang.

stages.owner: A local video game studio has made a game about crime in San Paro. It's sure to be a hit, so a crafty rival studio has paid us to help steal their idea. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>offices </Col>and <Col: StageText>take the data</Col>.
stages.dispatch: We're developing new software that can trace criminals by matching faces from CCTV feeds. Now the crooks want to use it to track us! <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>offices </Col>- don't let the crooks take the software.

stages.owner: I guess sometimes life really does imitate art. Crime in San Paro to steal a game about... Yeah. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>all of that <Col: StageText>data </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll get it to our clients.
stages.dispatch: The organized Crims in this city could give us major headaches with that stolen new software. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>that <Col: StageText>data </Col>before the perps get it to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Seems that most of the useful assets and data for the new video game are stored off-site. <Col: StageText>Rob </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and steal the PC on which that data is backed up.
stages.dispatch: The software those Criminals stole is only really dangerous if they get hold of our personnel files. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and stop them from stealing the PC on which that data is stored.

stages.owner: All right, we've agreed to make a direct hand-over of the PC. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>computer </Col>to the arranged <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll negotiate our payment. Maybe we can make Beta access part of the deal.
stages.dispatch: We need to keep that data secure, or the Criminals will be able to identify and trace our agents throughout the city. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them getting our <Col: StageText>computer </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Our payment is in this <Col: StageText>case </Col>but we got Enforcers all over us like white on rice. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before our opponents grab it and take it to theirs.

stages.dispatch: Damn. The Criminals transferred everything onto a <Col: StageText>laptop </Col>for portability's sake. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>it and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before they can get it to theirs. Gotta protect our personnel.

stages.owner: There's a dirty Tiger who's been trying to blackmail me, asking for money, and I want him dealt with. First <Col: StageText>burgle</Col> this <Col: StageText>building</Col> and steal his PDA.
stages.dispatch: We recently recovered some gold stolen by the Blood Roses, but the perps got away. Now they're after the evidence we have against them - <Col: StageText>defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>from burglars.

stages.owner: Right! Now <Col: StageText>deliver</Col> the <Col: StageText>PDA</Col> to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> and we'll check it over for anything we can use.
stages.dispatch: Our evidence against the Blood Roses is on that stolen <Col: StageText>PDA</Col>. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>it from being delivered to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Perfect - this idiot kept details of all of his "business" with San Paro gangs. <Col: StageText>Burgle</Col> this <Col: StageText>building</Col>. He's been stashing his gear there.
stages.dispatch: We couldn't find the rest of that bullion haul, but it looks like more Blood Roses are coming back for it. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>from them. The gold has to be stashed there.

stages.owner: The gold you just found was stolen during a recent raid - and now it's here, with his prints all over it! <Col: StageText>Deliver</Col> the <Col: StageText>gold</Col> to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> and we'll let the authorities know where they can find it.
stages.dispatch: That <Col: StageText>gold </Col>could fund all sorts of criminal activity. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>it from being delivered to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.dispatch: We can't allow those Blood Roses to get away with the proceeds of their crime. <Col: StageText>Capture this block</Col>.

missions.title: A BLOOD ROSE WITH A BADGE

stages.owner: The Enforcers have been working hard recently to win some hearts and minds. We need the public on our side. First, <Col: StageText>loot </Col>an Enforcer's <Col: StageText>car </Col>and take their <Col: StageText>ID Badge</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses have been spotted near an Enforcer's car - never a good sign. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and don't let them break into it.

stages.owner: Now that you got the badge, you can act like a 'Forcer. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>this random <Col: StageText>building</Col>, just like a Praetorian would. 'Confiscate' some 'evidence' - make it worth your while.
stages.dispatch: The Roses stole an Enforcer's badge from that car, and we fear they'll use it to stir up public opinion against us. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and don't let them fake an Enforcer raid on it.

stages.owner: Hey, this is fun - and legal! Well, kinda. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>another <Col: StageText>building</Col>. We'll make San Paro see the Enforcers as we know they are: uncouth thugs with badges.
stages.dispatch: With that badge, Blood Roses are masquerading as Enforcers. They're dragging our reputation through the dirt. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this civilian <Col: StageText>building </Col>before they can raid it.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>all that 'legally obtained' <Col: StageText>loot </Col>and the <Col: StageText>badge </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Jeung wants to make a big press event out of this.
stages.dispatch: The Roses stole money and goods from those properties. Even worse, they made it look like we did it. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we can prove our innocence.

stages.owner: Some Enforcers found out about your recent activities and are after you, big time. Or maybe they want to recruit you? Heh heh. <Col: StageText>Control the area</Col>to keep our subterfuge hushed up.
stages.dispatch: This could be a PR disaster. <Col: StageText>Capture this area</Col> and bring everyone involved to justice - that's the best way to rebuild our reputation with the citizens of San Paro.

stages.owner: Got an easy one for you here. A <Col: StageText>car </Col>was left unattended. Crack out your famous slim jim, <Col: StageText>break in</Col>, and <Col: StageText>take </Col>whatever you can <Col: StageText>find </Col>inside.
stages.dispatch: I left my Enforcer's badge in my car - again. Last time it nearly got taken. Can you check it out and <Col: StageText>protect my car</Col>? I don't want it being broken into.

stages.owner: Cool, a shiny new cop badge! Some SPPD rookie is gonna get busted. He even put his address on the back - what a noob. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>his <Col: StageText>building </Col>like you were a cop - and hey, see if he has any cash lying around.
stages.dispatch: Damn, G-Kings took my badge, and if they look on the back they'll find my address. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>my <Col: StageText>home </Col>and keep the Gs out of my shit - and my money!

stages.owner: A G-King who can't have fun winding up the cops is a G-King who's tired of life. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>the cop's <Col: StageText>office </Col>and grab his official SPPD phone: handy for calling in fake intel.
stages.dispatch: What the hell? The Gs broke in my house and are now probably heading for my undercover office. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>from being ransacked by G-King vandals.

stages.owner: Fuckin' sweet. We got his badge, his money and his phone. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>all those <Col: StageText>goodies </Col>to the G-King <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Bonita thinks she might be able to put them to good use.
stages.dispatch: This is a disaster. The G-Kings got my badge, my phone and my money. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and no one need be the wiser, eh, compadre?

stages.owner: Looks like the SPPD have called in 'Forcers to get their missing badge back; probably too embarrassed to do it themselves. <Col: StageText>Capture the area</Col>.
stages.dispatch: There's a simple way to solve this problem... Simple, yet effective. <Col: StageText>Capture this area </Col> before they get a chance to use my stolen badge illegally.

stages.owner: We're going to steal a whole armored truck full of cash. First step, <Col: StageText>sabotage </Col>these two <Col: StageText>ATMs </Col>and hide some gas pellets amongst the money. The security van will pick them up soon.
stages.dispatch: The Blood Roses are planning to hit these <Col: StageText>ATMs</Col> - I guess Charlotte Bloodrose must need a new pair of frilly panties. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the bank's machines from the Roses.

stages.owner: The driver unwittingly picked up our gas pellets, hidden in the ATM's money. He's unconscious, so get over there and <Col: StageText>steal </Col>the <Col: StageText>truck </Col>and all its cash.
stages.dispatch: Robbing the ATMs was a decoy. The Blood Roses' real target is the bank's security van that came to refill them. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>truck</Col>: it's a sitting duck out there.

stages.owner: The plan is working, in perfect Blood Rose style. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Bring the whole truck as well. 'Fortes fortuna adiuvat,' my friend.
stages.dispatch: The Roses have the <Col: StageText>security truck </Col>and all the cash it contains. If you can <Col: StageText>intercept </Col>them on the way back to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>, the bank may just forgive us - and pay us!

stages.owner: One of the money bags from the truck you stole has a tracking device in it. <Col: StageText>Get </Col>the <Col: StageText>money bag </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from the 'Forcers - and away from us.
stages.dispatch: Blood Roses? Dud Roses more like! They went and dropped one of the cash bags! <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep </Col>it away from them. We can use the money to draw them out into the open.

stages.owner: This war with the 'Forcers costs a fortune; we need cash for our upcoming property scam. <Col: StageText>Hack these ATMs </Col>so the bank'll think they're empty and send a truck fulla cash for us to steal.
stages.dispatch: We've been slowly turning up the heat on the G-Kings, cutting off their sources of revenue. They plan to hit these <Col: StageText>ATMs </Col>to get some fast cash. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the machines from being attacked.

stages.owner: Nice work, G. Your ATM hack fooled the bank into thinking their machines are empty; now an <Col: StageText>armored van </Col>is being filled with cash. Get there and <Col: StageText>steal </Col>it, and all the cash in the back.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings hacked the ATMs, sending a signal back to the bank that more bills are needed. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>security truck </Col>that was dispatched - it's full of replacement cash.

stages.owner: Now you need to <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. It will probably be easier if you just bring the truck in as well - more fun, too!
stages.dispatch: That <Col: StageText>truck </Col>is full of used bills, and the G-Kings are driving it to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them, or they'll have enough funds to wage a real war against us.

stages.owner: We've left your cut of the take nearby - <Col: StageText>recover </Col>your <Col: StageText>cash </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from the 'Forcers. If they want cash, they can hijack their own security van.
stages.dispatch: The G's have bagged up their stolen cash for ease of transport, and now we have a chance to catch them. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>money </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>out of their hands.

stages.owner: We're creating a highly potent tear gas but need two extra chemicals. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>the XS Drink Company <Col: StageText>building </Col>and get the first one. Watch out, it's extremely hazadous.
stages.dispatch: An inside source says the Blood Roses are trying to make some bad ass tear gas. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>as it contains a compound they'll need. <Col: StageText>Kill them </Col>if they resist.

stages.owner: Don't swallow it, it's what makes the drink green. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>of a company who make percussion grenades. They have the second chemical we need.
stages.dispatch: There is only one place the Roses can steal the other chemical they need for their tear gas. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and <Col: StageText>kill the Roses</Col>, rather than let them take the chemical.

stages.owner: Alright, now <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we can start making up some special Blood Rose tear gas.
stages.dispatch: The tear gas the Roses are planning to make will permiate even a gas mask. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the Roses before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>with their lethal cocktail of ingredients.

stages.owner: Shit! I spilt some and now I can't see. And it's eating through the floor, I think. You have to go <Col: StageText>burgle this pharmaceutical building </Col>and get me some stuff that might work as an antidote.
stages.dispatch: I saw gas escaping from the Roses lab. The idiots must have dropped their new tear gas. Schadenfreude in action! <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>pharmaceutical building </Col>and <Col: StageText>kill </Col>anyone who goes for the antidote.

stages.owner: You're a life saver. Now <Col: StageText>bring </Col>me the <Col: StageText>antidote </Col>via the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before I go blind. I'm never drinking XS again!
stages.dispatch: If the Roses have the tear gas and the antidote they will be a severe threat. So stop them now! <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> and confiscate the <Col: StageText>chemicals</Col>.

If the Roses have the tear gas and the antidote they will be a severe threat. So stop them now! <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> and confiscate the <Col: StageText>chemicals</Col>.

stages.owner: PNB bank have installed a new fingerprint scan security system. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>this morgue <Col: StageText>building </Col>and steal the finger of a security guard we killed last week. It is in their medical waste.
stages.dispatch: The fingerprint scanners in banks should have stopped the G-Kings. Instead they plan to steal a dead security guard's finger and use it. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>morgue </Col>from the Gs, or <Col: StageText>kill </Col>them.

stages.owner: We need the finger of a higher ranking employee to activate the vault fingerprint machine. Manager Lester Leffin is laid out at the forensics lab. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>and get that digit.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings need a second finger to fool the fingerprint machine at the bank vault. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>funeral parlor </Col>and the body of the bank's VP. If the Gs come, <Col: StageText>kill them</Col>, they are in the right place for it.

stages.owner: Alright, you can give the 'Forcers the finger - but only metaphorically. In reality you should <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>fingers </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Cheers.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings are making off with two dead <Col: StageText>fingers </Col>in those biohazard containers. They could get deep inside the bank vault with those. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The banks have ramped up their biometric security by introducing a retina scan. Luckily the late VP left her body to science. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>the <Col: StageText>office </Col>of the science lab.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings just realized the banks have installed a retina scanner. Now they need a bank manager's eyeball. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the medical <Col: StageText>lab</Col>. If the Gs show, <Col: StageText>kill them</Col>.

stages.owner: Good work. Now <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>that <Col: StageText>eyeball </Col>to the G-King <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Retinas are delicate, so keep an eye on it. Ha ha.
stages.dispatch: We can't let the criminals get away with all these body parts. Have they no respect? <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Collect their body parts and see how they like it.
We can't let the criminals get away with all these body parts. Have they no respect? <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col> and return it to ours.

stages.owner: Shock-jock Marta Riviera has been mouthing off about us again on her "WTF San Paro" show. <Col: StageText>Burn the sports cars </Col>belonging to her and her agent. That'll make for a great 'comment of the week'.
stages.dispatch: Shock-jock Marta Riviera made some decent pro-Enforcer comments on air, and the Criminals don't like it. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>sports cars </Col>that belong to her and her agent, and we may get another mention.

stages.owner: You know, it's wrong to blame Marta for calling us 'thugs' on that radio show, she is just part of the system. So <Col: StageText>set fire </Col>to the radio station owner's <Col: StageText>office </Col>instead.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>from arsonists. It belongs to the radio station that has been giving us some top publicity recently. A good job here will help our recruiting process.

stages.owner: Looks like the radio station has hired some help. Here's the headline - <Col: StageText>kill them all</Col>. And tune in next week, folks, for more extreme violence!
stages.dispatch: Marta Riviera's radio station has hired us to take care of their Criminal 'critics'. <Col: StageText>Kill everyone </Col>who doesn't understand that you phone in your comments - you don't take it out on the staff.

stages.owner: Food guru Akira Watanabe borrowed a large sum of money from us to launch a new restaurant. Repayment has not been forthcoming. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>his <Col: StageText>sports cars </Col>as a gentle reminder.
stages.dispatch: Food guru Akira Watanabe needs some personal protection. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>his <Col: StageText>cars </Col>from being bombed by a gang of Criminals. They want to use his restaurant as a front.

stages.owner: Still no repayments from Watanabe-san. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>these two <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>; his storerooms. Hope he likes BBQ.
stages.dispatch: Heads up! Akira Watanabe's properties are now also at risk. <Col: StageText>Protect the buildings </Col>from the Criminal bombers. Maybe Akira's food was too rich for their delicate sensibilities.

stages.owner: Akira Wantanbe has hired in some extra protection. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>any <Col: StageText>opponents</Col>, and I'll go visit him in person to get our money back. Revenge is a dish best served cold.
stages.dispatch: This gang really want to get to Akira Watanabe. He stood up to the Criminals and we have to support him. <Col: StageText>Kill his enemies</Col>, and Watanabe could become a powerful pro-Enforcer advocate in San Paro.

stages.owner: Two reporters have been sniffing around, looking for a scoop on San Paro's "seedy underbelly." Well, go give them an exclusive. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>their undercover <Col: StageText>offices</Col>, and take anything that may incriminate us.
stages.dispatch: A couple of local reporters were sent a photo that links a local gang with the recent ram-raid of the Karnak Casino. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>their undercover <Col: StageText>offices </Col>until we can recover that evidence.

stages.owner: Shit, those are guns we used on a recent job. I guess the reporters dug them out of a dumpster somewhere. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>those <Col: StageText>guns </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll get rid of them - properly, this time.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals have recovered the photographic evidence linking them to the casino robbery. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>that <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>before the Criminals get it to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: I'm concerned that those reporters might have more intel on the job we pulled. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>their editor's <Col: StageText>office </Col>and see if there's anything else that could be used against us.
stages.dispatch: These reporters could teach our investigators a thing or two. They have footage of the Criminals committing the robbery. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the editor's <Col: StageText>office </Col>from any attempt to steal that film.

stages.owner: Shit, that camcorder footage shows our whole job. At least they got my good side. Still, <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>footage </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and I'll keep it with my personal collection.
stages.dispatch: That <Col: StageText>camcorder </Col>carries footage that will nail our case against those Criminals. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them <Col: StageText>delivering </Col>it to their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>or it'll be gone for good.

stages.owner: Damn, the reporters must have sent their article to the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>.
stages.dispatch: Without that camcorder, our case is shaky. We need the Crims out of this area so we can search for new evidence. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>.

missions.title: THAT TV'S BIGGER THAN MY HOUSE

stages.owner: We need a big-ass ride to transport some merchandise. <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>this <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and I'll suggest that we only acquire plasma screens smaller than 70 inches from now on.
stages.dispatch: A local gang are going to rob a big electronics shipping company, but they need something to transport the humongous plasma TVs. <Col: StageText>Protect this vehicle</Col>, they want to use it to transport them.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver that vehicle</Col>. We'll change the plates, then it can be sent out on our TV removal job. We can fit a lot of screens in the back of that beast.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>that <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>before it reaches the gang's <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>point. Without it, they can't pull off their planned robbery.

stages.owner: Even that vehicle won't be big enough on its own. <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>this <Col: StageText>van</Col> - it should have the capacity to take a few stolen 120 inch jumbo plasmas.
stages.dispatch: This gang means serious business. They are going to steal a van so they can take the largest plasma TVs. Must be planning a helluva Superbowl party this year! <Col: StageText>Don't let them steal the van</Col>.

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Deliver the van </Col>so we can get it ready. I may need to up the suspension on it if these plasmas are as heavy as I've heard.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>that <Col: StageText>van </Col>from reaching the gang's <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>point. That will put an end to their whole plasma TV heist.

stages.owner: Somebody leaked our plans to shift the plasma TVs. <Col: StageText>Hold </Col>our drop-off<Col: StageText>area </Col>.
stages.dispatch: If that's how they want to play it, then it's time to deliver some big screen justice, HD style. Take <Col: StageText>hold </Col> of the <Col: StageText>area </Col>.

stages.owner: We just killed Asenka Leonov, a member of the Russian Mafia. Not good - now we need cash to buy off witnesses. <Col: StageText>Set fire </Col>to these target <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>to scare up some protection money.
stages.dispatch: An ex-KGB officer - Asenka Leonov - and her gang of Russian Mafiosos are running a protection racket. They're planning an <Col: StageText>arson </Col>attack on these civilian <Col: StageText>vehicles</Col>. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the vehicles.

stages.owner: A couple of property owners won't pay protection 'cause their buildings are safeguarded by a sprinkler system. Cut the power to their block by <Col: StageText>sabotaging </Col>these <Col: StageText>electrical boxes</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Leonov has now ordered her gang to <Col: StageText>sabotage </Col>these <Col: StageText>electrical boxes</Col>. This may be an attempt to disable the fire alarms and sprinklers in nearby buildings.<Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the sabotage.

stages.owner: With the power down, the sprinkler systems are inactive. Now's the time to <Col: StageText>burn </Col>these <Col: StageText>properties</Col>. We'll start hitting up the neighbors, suggesting the same thing could happen to them...
stages.dispatch: The gang escalated their <Col: StageText>arson </Col>attack, moving onto these <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>them, and show the citizens that we can protect them.

stages.owner: The neigboring property owners are paying up. You've done well, but you've drawn unwanted attention. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>all <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>- we need to pay off the witnesses to the Leonov killing ASAP.
stages.dispatch: The arson attempts by Asenka Leonov and her gang of Russian Mafia have been successful, but we can still salvage something - <Col: StageText>eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>arsonists </Col>as a deterrent against future attacks.

stages.owner: A gang smuggling fire opals stashed some gems nearby, but we don't know where. <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>the <Col: StageText>information </Col>from this<Col: StageText> building </Col>- Enforcers are using it as a base to investigate the smugglers.
stages.dispatch: Our investigation into a gang smuggling Mexican fire opals is based in this <Col: StageText>building</Col>. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the building from burglary - the gang is trying to steal our intel.

stages.owner: Bring that Enforcer <Col: StageText>paperwork </Col>to this <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll try and figure out what we need to know. Those fire opals will be worth a fortune on the open market.
stages.dispatch: Our <Col: StageText>intel </Col>on that opal smuggling gang is on its way to this <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>- be sure to <Col: StageText>stop </Col>it before it arrives. We were just about to bust the whole international operation...

stages.owner: Excellent. The Enforcers had located the stash of stolen opals but needed a CSA order for recovery. Move in fast and <Col: StageText>steal </Col>what you can from these <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>, before the Enforcers raid them.
stages.dispatch: The gang know we're on to them - they're trying to retrieve an opal shipment from these <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>. Be sure to <Col: StageText>defend </Col>the buildings from attempted burglary. We need to recover those gems!

stages.owner: Bring those <Col: StageText>fire opals </Col>to this <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>while we arrange to sell them on to the highest bidder. Several collectors, sculptors and jewelers have already expressed an interest.
stages.dispatch: The gang of smugglers raided those storage buildings. Make sure you <Col: StageText>stop </Col>the <Col: StageText>fire opals </Col>they've taken from being delivered to this <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Excellent. One phone call, and we've got a bundle of cash in exchange for those fire opals. <Col: StageText>Grab </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from any opponents.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Grab </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>paid by international buyers for those opals. <Col: StageText>Keep it </Col>out of the gang's hands. We can still make a case against the gang if we can trace the money.

stages.owner: We've been paid to steal national security information. It's held in a case with a digital combination lock. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and recover the case and the PDA holding the combination.
stages.dispatch: Burglars are targeting these <Col: StageText>offices</Col>. They're trying to steal classified information about off-shore naval operations. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the offices, and keep the data out of Criminal hands.

stages.owner: We've been paid to steal national security information. It's held in a case with a digital combination lock. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and recover the case and the PDA holding the combination.
stages.dispatch: Burglars are targeting these <Col: StageText>offices</Col>. They're trying to steal classified information about off-shore naval operations. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the offices and keep the data out of Criminal hands.

stages.owner: Great! You have the <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>and the <Col: StageText>combination</Col>. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>both items to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll get the case open. Our buyers will be most financially grateful.
stages.dispatch: Criminals have stolen a <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>and a <Col: StageText>PDA </Col>holding the keycode to get the briefcase open. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Criminals before they get everything to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Damn! We only got half of that classified information. The rest is in a different case with a different PDA code combination. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and take the second PDA and case.
stages.dispatch: Naval Intelligence says the second half of that classified information is in these <Col: StageText>offices</Col>. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the offices from the burglars and keep the data out of their hands.

stages.owner: Damn! We only got half of that classified information. The rest is in a different case with a different PDA code combination. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and take the second PDA and case.
stages.dispatch: Naval Intelligence says the second half of that classified information is in these <Col: StageText>offices</Col>. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the offices from the burglars and keep the data out of their hands.

stages.owner: Our espionage is about to be very successful: <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the second <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>and the <Col: StageText>combination </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll complete our analysis.
stages.dispatch: Criminals have the second <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>and the <Col: StageText>PDA </Col>with the code to open it. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Criminals before they get everything to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Good work. We've compiled the national security information and uploaded it directly to our foreign clients. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>our <Col: StageText>payment </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>it away from our opponents.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals have uploaded the data they've stolen, but have yet to collect payment from their foreign buyers. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>payment </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>on to it - we may be able to trace its source.

stages.owner: Enforcers have shut down our usual sources of explosives, so we need to kick it home-brew style. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>this shipping <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and steal a canister of nitric acid.
stages.dispatch: We've confiscated large quantities of explosives from local gangs. They'll probably now try to make their own. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>crate </Col>of nitric acid: it's a key ingredient.

stages.owner: Methyl-B is a little harder to come by, but we've found a small stash belonging to another gang. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>that <Col: StageText>building </Col>and take the chemical.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals will now be looking to acquire a solvent for their home-made explosives, and we've located a vulnerable source in this <Col: StageText>building</Col>. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the target from the burglars.

stages.owner: Lastly, we need some detonators. An explosives expert, Azrael, ram-raided an electronics store. He locked stolen <Col: StageText>detonators </Col>in the back of the <Col: StageText>van </Col>he used. <Col: StageText>Break in </Col>and take them.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals now need detonators for their home-made bombs. A shipment of electronics is in transit via this van. <Col: StageText>Protect the van </Col>from these modern day Alfred Nobels.

stages.owner: Now <Col: StageText>deliver everything </Col>back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll mix it up. I got a few 'expendable' guys doing the actual chemistry, since I guess you enjoy having all your fingers as much as I do.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals are now taking all of the bomb <Col: StageText>components </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>that delivery, or we'll be on the other end of those explosives.

stages.owner: We need to test the mix, and you probably to see the results of all your hard work. <Col: StageText>Bomb </Col>these <Col: StageText>garages </Col>and show the Enforcers we're coming for them.
stages.dispatch: The Criminals have built a couple of small bombs and are going to test their home-made explosive mix. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>garages</Col>and prevent the terror attacks on the populace.

stages.owner: The mix is good, and we're ready to make a statement: everyone has a right to high explosives, here in San Paro. Plant a <Col: StageText>bomb </Col>in this public <Col: StageText>area </Col>and then <Col: StageText>protect it</Col> until it explodes.
stages.dispatch: A third, more complex, device has been built, and the Criminals want to use it in a <Col: StageText>public area</Col>. Needier for attention than kindergarteners. <Col: StageText>Protect the area </Col>and <Col: StageText>defuse the bomb </Col>if they arm it.

stages.owner: I've got some low-profile crews out in the city, keeping watch on 'Forcers, scoping out future jobs, keeping me in the loop. They're due to be paid. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and grab some cash.
stages.dispatch: An employee at a client's company embezzled funds to pay for her wedding, and hired thugs to get rid of her paper trail. <Col: StageText>Defend this building </Col>before they take a magnet to the PCs in there.

stages.owner: That should be enough cash to pay for the information from my first crew of intel-gatherers, but we'll need more. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>another <Col: StageText>building </Col>and get hold of some more cash.
stages.dispatch: That bride would have gotten away with her embezzling - but she screwed up and made a transaction in the wrong currency. <Col: StageText>Defend this building </Col>from her thugs before they shred her files.

stages.owner: The third crew gets a bonus: they gave me good intel for a couple of your jobs. What, you never wondered how I always know what's up? <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>this gang's <Col: StageText>stash </Col>and steal all of it.
stages.dispatch: The embezzling bride has been laundering money for months, and now has cash stashes in several places. <Col: StageText>Defend this building </Col>from the Crims she hired so they can't retrieve that dough.

stages.owner: All right, that's enough cash to pay everyone. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>some of the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and the first crew will collect it from there.
stages.dispatch: Thanks to all the embezzlement, the bride could order imported orchids for every centerpiece. Her florist was willing to be paid under the table. <Col: StageText>Stop her payment reaching this drop-off. </Col>

stages.owner: Two crews' paydays left. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>some more of the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location</Col>, and that'll be enough for the second crew. They'll dole it out.
stages.dispatch: Our client's embezzling employee is getting some local pyro to set off a huge fireworks display during the reception - not cheap... <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>her guys reaching their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>with the pyro's payment.

stages.owner: Just the third crew needs to be paid now. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and they'll work out the split amongst themselves.
stages.dispatch: More <Col: StageText>cash </Col>is on its way to a <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>to bribe a hotel desk jockey. He's going to book rooms for the bride's wedding guests. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the bride's hired thugs before they make that delivery.

stages.owner: My boys have been busy again! This <Col: StageText>case </Col>contains intelligence which will help me plan future jobs. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before the Enforcers get it to theirs.

stages.dispatch: The bride's thugs collected a <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>full of Strigoi sunglasses for wedding favors. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll use it as evidence against this crazy broad.

stages.owner: G-Kings have been selling pirated video games; games published by companies under Praetorian protection. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>where the copies are being made.
stages.dispatch: We've made quite a bit of cash selling pirated video games and now the Praetorians are on to us. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>our <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and ensure that the 'Torians don't <Col: StageText>raid </Col>them.

stages.owner: Good work. Now <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>games </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll take them in as evidence.

stages.owner: It seems that pirated copies of the latest Super Highway Patrol game are being sold from the back of vehicles around the city. <Col: StageText>Search </Col>this <Col: StageText>van </Col>for any evidence.
stages.dispatch: We were selling pirated copies of the latest Super Highway Patrol game from the back of this<Col: StageText> van</Col>: now it's a Praetorian target. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the van from Praetorian investigation.

stages.owner: That <Col: StageText>bag </Col>contains cash earned through the sale of pirated goods. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the cash to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians took the cash from our pirated game dealers! We need it to fund our new stock of diamond-studded grenades. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>before it reaches the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The G-Kings are trying to prevent seizure of 100,000 copies of Super Higway Patrol, by torching the evidence! <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the storage <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>. Protect any evidence that survives the fires.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians are about to shut this piracy operation down, so we'll need to cover our tracks. <Col: StageText>Burn </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>containing the last pieces of evidence. <Col:StageText>Recover anything not burned.</Col>

stages.owner: That <Col: StageText>bag </Col>contains cash earned through the sale of pirated games. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the cash to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Remember, kids: piracy funds terrorism... and poseurs like the Blood Roses.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers took the cash we got from selling pirated games! We need it to fund some of our more ambitious plans, like the petting zoo heist. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>from reaching their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: The software pirates are seeking to prevent our investigation of their properties. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from the <Col: StageText>arsonists</Col>.

stages.owner: A valuable painting owned by Choi Ji-Sung was stolen from a lockup whilst awaiting restoration. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>the <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>for anything that might provide a suspect.
stages.dispatch: We stole a painting from a lockup where it was being restored. The owner paid some Enforcers to investigate. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>storehouse </Col>from their investigators.

stages.owner: Fingerprints from the scene match those of a local art thief. We have him registered as retired. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>his <Col: StageText>home </Col>and <Col: StageText>workplace </Col>for anything that appears suspicious.
stages.dispatch: Damn, it looks like our guys must've got sloppy. The Enforcers are heading to a couple of our <Col: StageText>hideouts</Col>. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>those buildings from the Enforcer raids.

stages.dispatch: Damn, it looks like our guys must've got sloppy. The Enforcers are heading to a couple of our <Col: StageText>hideouts</Col>. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>those buildings from the Enforcer raids.

stages.owner: We found breaching <Col: StageText>explosives </Col>and <Col: StageText>boltcutters</Col>. Looks like our art thief is back in business. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the evidence to our <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>while we track him down.
stages.dispatch: Shit, the Enforcers found the <Col: StageText>explosives </Col>and <Col: StageText>boltcutters </Col>used during the theft. Someone's gonna get a verbal lashing! You need to <Col: StageText>stop </Col>that evidence from reaching the Enforcer <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: We've picked up the thief and a street patrol has located his <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>. <Col: StageText>Search </Col>the car. The painting was probably stashed there, ready for a quick getaway.
stages.dispatch: The jackass who stole the painting was picked up by the Enforcers. Thankfully, he left the loot stashed in his car for exactly this situation. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>that <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>from the Enforcers.

stages.owner: Great. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>painting </Col>back to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. I'm no art lover, but Miss Ji-Sung was adamant that it be kept in one piece. Try not to get shot at.
stages.dispatch: Shit, the Enforcers have the <Col: StageText>painting </Col>we stole and they're heading back to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them before they get the painting there.

stages.owner: Ah, hell. That drop-off is too hot and Criminals are startin' to swarm. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>painting </Col>to our secondary <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>- and don't let the Criminals take it to theirs.

stages.dispatch: All right! You've pressured the Enforcers so much they're headed for a secondary location. Keep it up! <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>painting </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>it back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before they can get it to theirs.

stages.owner: A shipment of lethal nerve gas was hijacked and we need to recover it. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>this <Col: StageText>device</Col>. It can detect down to 1 mg / m3 of the chemical.
stages.dispatch: We stole nerve gas from a company trying to sneak it into San Paro. Now the Praetorians have been called in to find it. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the chemical <Col: StageText>detector </Col>they'll need.

stages.owner: You need to triangulate the nerve gas by taking a range of readings. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>detector </Col>to the first of three <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and scan for chemical traces.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians are trying to triangulate the position of our nerve gas. It's safer in our hands - which is saying something! <Col: StageText>Stop them getting</Col> the chemical <Col: StageText>detector </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location</Col>.

stages.owner: That's one scan complete. Now <Col: StageText>take </Col>the <Col: StageText>detector </Col>to the second <Col: StageText>location </Col>and scan from there. This is what the Praetorians do best: rise to the challenge of city-wide chaos.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Praetorians <Col: StageText>taking </Col>the chemical detector to this second <Col: StageText>triangulation point</Col>. They not looking for the gas to protect the public - they just want to sell it to the highest bidder.

stages.owner: One more scan will allow us to triangulate the location of the nerve gas accurately. <Col: StageText>Go to </Col>the third <Col: StageText>location </Col>and use the <Col: StageText>detector </Col>there. Hurry. We need to recapture this deadly compound.
stages.dispatch: God knows where this nerve gas was originally headed - to be used by a dictator against his people, maybe. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the corporate lapdogs from <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>their final detection <Col: StageText>location</Col>.

stages.owner: Praetorian Tech HQ has a reading - faint, but it's there. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>nerve gas </Col>before anyone can put it to use.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians have triangulated the location of the <Col: StageText>nerve gas</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them before they can <Col: StageText>pick it up</Col>. They can't be trusted with it.

stages.owner: Good work. San Paro can rest easier with those <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>safe in Praetorian hands. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>them to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll deal with them properly.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>that <Col: StageText>nerve gas </Col>before the Praetorians <Col: StageText>take it back </Col>to their corporate masters. They'll sell it to the first dictator with a big enough wallet - and they call us Criminals!

stages.owner: Shit - Praetorian Tech HQ has discovered a second container, shielded from detection. It's enough gas to wipe out a city block. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>barrel </Col>and don't let anyone get in your way.
stages.dispatch: Damn - the 'Forcers took the canister, but the bulk of the nerve gas is in a barrel nearby. Get there fast and <Col: StageText>pick up the barrel </Col>before the Praetorians do.

stages.owner: This is a priority one task. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>nerve gas </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>it to our HazMat <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. The gangs are after you - they could hold San Paro to ransom with that much Sarin.

stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>nerve gas barrel </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off.</Col> Don't let the Praetorians hand it over to their corporate bosses. Who knows what they'll do with it?

missions.title: MY, GRAMMA, HOW YOUNG YOU LOOK

stages.owner: A shipment of ultra expensive Botox has been stolen. The office is getting a barrage of phone calls from concerned Prentiss ladies. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>this <Col: StageText>detector </Col>which can sniff out the protein.
stages.dispatch: We stole Botox; way easy to move, and worth more per ounce than heroin. The Tigers found out. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them from <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the chemical detector they'll need to find it.

stages.owner: We need to triangulate the readings to track down the stolen Botox. My mom is freaking out that there'll be a shortage. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>detector </Col>to the first of three <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and scan for traces.
stages.dispatch: The Prentiss Tigers are trying to triangulate the position of our stolen Botox. <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>getting to </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>with their detector.

stages.owner: That's one scan complete. Now <Col: StageText>take </Col>the <Col: StageText>detector </Col>to the second of the three <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and scan again for the Botox. Be quick - they're rioting down at the nip/tuck clinic.
stages.dispatch: The Prentiss Tigers are using the detector to scan for the Botox we took. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Tigers from <Col: StageText>taking </Col>the detector to the next <Col: StageText>location</Col>.

stages.owner: One more scan with the detector will allow us to triangulate the position. <Col: StageText>Get over </Col>to the third <Col: StageText>location </Col>while we're young. Or we'll need the Botox ourselves!
stages.dispatch: The Tigers seem more intent on recovering this Botox than that mustard gas we took last week. Guess Mommy doesn't need mustard gas... <Col: StageText>Stop them </Col>from <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>the final <Col: StageText>triangulation point</Col>.

stages.owner: We have a reading - but it's as faint as the wrinkles on my granny's Botoxed forehead. Get over there and <Col: StageText>recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>chemical </Col>before the place is swarming with washed-up celebs.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers know where our Botox is stashed and are eager to get their hands on it. Maybe they're all actually in their 50s! <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them before they make the <Col: StageText>pickup</Col>.

stages.owner: Great work. I always said you were more than a good-looking face. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the Botox to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Sofia has been showing a lot of interest... for *some* reason.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers have the Botox. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>them before they reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Remember, one side effect can be twitching - so they may have loose trigger fingers.

stages.owner: Damn, we're picking up a second reading. I think that first container was just to throw us off the scent. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the larger Botox <Col: StageText>container</Col>. It must be worth a fortune.
stages.dispatch: The Tigers almost fell for our plan. We let them take a small container of Botox so we could keep the main container. Get to it fast and <Col: StageText>pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>barrel </Col>before the Tigers find it.

stages.owner: This is getting a lot of TV coverage, so don't fuck it up now. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>barrel </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. You could spill a bit on the sidewalk; cover up those cracks.

stages.dispatch: Are the Tigers frowning because we got their Botox? ...I can't tell! Heh heh. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>barrel </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver it </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We'll sell it back to those Prentiss biddies at a markup.

stages.dispatch: Enforcers are moving through our turf. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them from covering up our <Col: StageText>tags</Col>. I'll try to find out what those losers are up to.

stages.owner: Let's get the neighborhood looking tidy. <Col: StageText>Cover </Col>the gang <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>at these locations and then <Col: StageText>protect </Col>them from further attacks. If you don't, the writing's on the wall - for us.
stages.dispatch: More of our territory is at risk. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>from Enforcers and <Col: StageText>re-spray </Col>them if necessary. 'Forcers are just posing to look good for a municipal CSA inspector.

stages.owner: If the CSA inspector sees this, he'll cut our budget. <Col: StageText>Cover </Col>the last two locations and then <Col: StageText>protect </Col>them. The gangs will be trying to embarrass us on purpose.
stages.dispatch: I bet the city officials will love our graffiti... <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>our <Col: StageText>spots </Col>from Enforcers who want to cover up our tags. <Col: StageText>Re-spray</Col> them if necessary.

stages.owner: Now we need to hold this territory, ready for the CSA inspection. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these locations and then <Col: StageText>defend </Col>them.
stages.dispatch: It's time to evict the Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>them to defend our turf. The city CSA official should be made aware: this is OUR patch of San Paro.

stages.dispatch: We've just bought the deeds to some properties, expanding our territory. Now Enforcers are covering our graffiti and moving onto our new turf. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>our <Col: StageText>tags</Col> from those toy soldiers.

stages.owner: There's more graffiti on this nearby block. <Col: StageText>Clean up</Col> the gang tags while we draw their attention. You can always rely on Criminals to be vain and try to re-tag those spots eventually.
stages.dispatch: More of our <Col: StageText>tags </Col>are under threat. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>them from the Enforcers. They're still pissed at us for expanding our territory, and they want revenge.

stages.owner: We have four potential targets, but we don't know exactly where the stolen deeds are. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and <Col: StageText>recover </Col>both property <Col: StageText>deeds</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Now our safehouses are at risk - <Col: StageText>defend </Col>each of these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>from Enforcer raids. They're after the property deeds we just acquired.

stages.owner: Excellent - we have what we came for. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>those <Col: StageText>deeds </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. The gang will have to find another way to expand its empire.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers have taken our property deeds. They can't stand to see us developing and expanding. <Col: StageText>Don't </Col>let the 'Forcers <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>deeds </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Okay, that gang's pissed. We rattled their cage, so we expected this: <Col: StageText>eliminate </Col>those <Col: StageText>Criminals </Col>before they take you down.
stages.dispatch: We tried expanding our empire officially, but it seems the Enforcers don't play by the rules they claim to uphold. <Col: StageText>Wipe out </Col>the <Col: StageText>Enforcers</Col>. We tried to play it their way; now they can play it ours.

stages.owner: The Montebank cartel is trying to destroy its rival's shipment of SMGs, but we need it as evidence. They've planted a <Col: StageText>bomb </Col>in a van parked nearby - get there and <Col: StageText>defuse </Col>it, fast!
stages.dispatch: We've gotta burn that last shipment of SMGs, or we'll be put away for years. Enforcers are headed towards the van and the incendiary we planted. <Col: StageText>Don't let them defuse it</Col>.

stages.owner: The bomb was stashed inside this <Col: StageText>case</Col>. Bring it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll analyze it. We may be able to pin other crimes on that Montebank cartel, if they've used similar devices in the past.
stages.dispatch: Now the Enforcers are taking the <Col: StageText>bomb </Col>to be analyzed; <Col: StageText>stop </Col>them <Col: StageText>taking </Col>it to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We've made others like it, so it's bound to implicate us in other crimes.

stages.owner: A member of the Montebank cartel was seen fleeing the crime scene. They dropped a <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>which may contain valuable evidence. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>it to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and prevent the cartel taking it to theirs.

stages.dispatch: This <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>contains information about our entire gun smuggling operation, our Yard contacts, the works. <Col: StageText>Take it </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and stop the Enforcers taking it to theirs.

stages.owner: A gang has been using payphones to take illegal bets; they must have discovered that we can trace their cell phones. <Col: StageText>Bug </Col>this <Col: StageText>payphone </Col>that they regularly use.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are onto our numbers-running sideline. I bet they'll try to bug the payphone we use for our business - not that I'm a gambler, of course! Anyway, <Col: StageText>protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>payphone</Col>.

stages.owner: We need more proof of illegal bookmaking activity before we can move against the gang. <Col: StageText>Bug two </Col>more <Col: StageText>payphones </Col>they regularly use.
stages.dispatch: We've switched payphones, as the 'Forcers bugged the usual one we use to take our bets. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the Enforcers from <Col: StageText>planting bugs </Col>on these <Col: StageText>payphones </Col>too.

stages.owner: Our bugged phones just paid off! A gang member let slip the locations of their illegal betting offices. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>these <Col: StageText>properties </Col>and take the <Col: StageText>betting slips </Col>you find to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are onto our whole bookmaking operation. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>our <Col: StageText>offices </Col>against raids and <Col: StageText>stop </Col>any <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>from reaching the 'Forcer <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: That illegal gambling info you got us shows the gang must use a central database to track all the bets. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>their <Col: StageText>laptop </Col>and then <Col: StageText>hold on to it </Col>while we download the data via 3G.
stages.dispatch: Damn. Our numbers runner was wounded and dropped his <Col: StageText>laptop</Col> - all our betting accounts are stored on there! <Col: StageText>Get it </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from the Enforcers.

stages.owner: Identity theft is rife in this area. 'Skimming' devices are often planted on ATMs to record a citizen's card details. <Col: StageText>Examine </Col>the first <Col: StageText>ATM </Col>for such a device.
stages.dispatch: We've called in some experitise to help attach skimming devices to ATMs. It's the best way to get a lot of bank details, fast! Enforcers are <Col: StageText>searching this ATM </Col>for one of our devices. <Col: StageText>Stop them</Col>!

stages.owner: No luck. However, the second <Col: StageText>ATM </Col>is located here. <Col: StageText>Examine </Col>it thoroughly. You wouldn't want the Criminals tampering with *your* slot, would you?
stages.dispatch: Enforcers are getting closer to finding one of the devices we're using to steal bank account details. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them <Col: StageText>searching </Col>any more <Col: StageText>ATMs</Col>.

stages.owner: Still nothing! But I know ID theft is going on out there. I doubt poor old Mrs. Mills really spent ten grand at the Karnak Casino. There's another <Col: StageText>ATM </Col>here; <Col: StageText>check it out </Col>too.
stages.dispatch: This <Col: StageText>ATM </Col>is fitted with one of our skimming devices for stealing bank card details. <Col: StageText>Don't let the Enforcers examine it</Col>! We borrowed the device from some techie friends.

stages.owner: Got one! <Col: StageText>Bring </Col>the skimming <Col: StageText>device </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location </Col>for analysis. There are only a few people in San Paro who can actually make such a device.
stages.dispatch: The 'Forcers have one of our ATM skimming <Col: StageText>devices</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them taking it to their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>for analysis. We need to return it to our high-tech experts.

stages.owner: The device is similar to one we recovered last week. Forensics  linked it to a local gang operating out of this <Col: StageText>building</Col>. Get there and <Col: StageText>raid </Col>the place.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers have traced the ATM skimmer back to us. <Col: StageText>Protect our offices </Col>from being raided. Don't let them recover anything that could incriminate us.

stages.owner: The identity thieves already booked it, but there're enough stolen credit card details here to buy the WP tower! <Col: StageText>Bring </Col>the key <Col: StageText>evidence </Col>you find <Col: StageText>here</Col>.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers found all our stolen credit card details. They packaged it up as <Col: StageText>evidence</Col>. <Col: StageText>Don't let them </Col>get it to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: We believe the identity thieves are trying to flee the area. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and then <Col: StageText>hold </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>to prevent their escape, while we move in on them.
stages.dispatch: We need to get our techie guys out of here so they can continue the ATM scam elsewhere in San Paro. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and then <Col: StageText>hold </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>on their escape route.

stages.owner: One of our key political supporters had his car stolen and wants it back. First, <Col: StageText>track </Col>the vehicle's GPS locator <Col: StageText>through </Col>this <Col: StageText>satellite</Col>.
stages.dispatch: I stole a sweeeet ride, and I want to keep it for myself. The Enforcers sent a whole team out after it - that's how cool it is. <Col: StageText>Defend this satellite </Col>dish, so they can't trace the car's GPS.

stages.owner: The car is being driven by a local gang leader, who's keeping it as a trophy. Lure him out by <Col: StageText>covering </Col>the gang <Col: StageText>tags </Col>on his turf. See how he likes us messing with his stuff!
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Don't </Col>let the Enforcers <Col: StageText>cover our tags </Col>or the whole gang will be drawn into this. I stole that car just for me, and they'd all want a cruise in it.

stages.owner: We know the gang leader hates anyone touching his 'art' - had three graffiti removal teams killed nearby last month alone. Continue to <Col: StageText>covering </Col>the <Col: StageText>tags </Col>in this area until he's lured out of hiding.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Don't </Col>let the Enforcers <Col: StageText>cover </Col>up more of our <Col: StageText>tags</Col>. They just want to draw us out into the open. Jeez, you steal one car and suddenly everyone is up in your grill.

stages.owner: There - the vehicle has been moved and he's meeting with his lieutenants. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>while it's unattended.
stages.dispatch: Damn, they found my sweet ride. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>my <Col: StageText>car</Col>! I just fitted new speakers. They were so solid I had to up the suspension. That's how heavy my sound is, baby!

stages.owner: <Col: StageText>Bring the vehicle </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location</Col>. We'll arrange to return it to its original owner. He may want to de-pimp his ride though.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are moving my <Col: StageText>ride </Col>to a safe <Col: StageText>location</Col>. <Col: StageText>Don't let them </Col>get it there. Those dudes won't appreciate the solid marble dashboard I had installed.

stages.owner: Our benefactor has provided us with some additional funding, thanks to your good work. It's in this case. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>case </Col>and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from any gang members - who have to walk home now! Ha ha.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers took my ride - and I know why. There was a hefty reward for it's return to the original owner. <Col: StageText>Get to </Col>the <Col: StageText>case </Col>full of reward money first, and <Col: StageText>keep it </Col>away from them.

stages.owner: We picked up Azrael bragging about a bomb he'd planted, but the prick won't tell us where it is. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>his <Col: StageText>base </Col>of operations.
stages.dispatch: Itchy - one of our bombing crew - was careless and got picked up. Now he's squealing like a bitch to any Enforcer who'll listen. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>our old <Col: StageText>hideout </Col>from the Enforcer bomb squad.

stages.owner: Nothing solid on location, but it looks like Azrael's using a cellphone trigger for his device. <Col: StageText>Hack </Col>this telecom satellite <Col: StageText>uplink </Col>- we're going to track the phone signal from the bomb.
stages.dispatch: Itchy blabbed about the bombs we planted, but didn't know where the last one was. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this telecom satellite <Col: StageText>uplink </Col>- the Enforcers may use it to locate the bomb's cellphone detonator.

stages.owner: There's another telecom satellite <Col: StageText>uplink </Col>in this area. <Col: StageText>Hack </Col>it quickly, and we'll be one step closer to narrowing down the location of Azrael's bomb.
stages.dispatch: Now the Enforcers know about our bomb, they're trying to trace its cellphone detonator. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this telecom satellite <Col: StageText>uplink </Col>until the bomb explodes.

stages.owner: All right, this last satellite <Col: StageText>uplink </Col>will let us triangulate the position of the bomb's cell-phone detonator. <Col: StageText>Hack </Col>it - and hope we can get to the bomb in time!
stages.dispatch: If the Enforcers complete their hack into this last telecom satellite <Col: StageText>uplink </Col>they'll be able to track the detonator on our bomb. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>it until the bomb explodes.

stages.owner: We've found the <Col: StageText>bomb</Col>. Get to it quickly, and <Col: StageText>disarm </Col>it before it blows!
stages.dispatch: It looks like the Enforcers have found our bomb and are gearing up to defuse it. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>bomb </Col>until it explodes.

stages.owner: Shit, that was a chemical bomb. Real nasty. Azrael's going down for this! Recover the <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>for analysis. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>them to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before the Criminals can take them to theirs.

stages.dispatch: The Enforcers have defused our bomb and are taking components as evidence. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>those volatile <Col: StageText>chemicals </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before the Enforcers get them to theirs.

stages.owner: Things have been quiet in this area - maybe too quiet. Head out into the neighborhood, <Col: StageText>cover-up </Col>any <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>you find, and keep an eye open for anything suspicious.
stages.dispatch: A few Enforcers are hanging around, pretending to care about graffiti - but they're probably staking us out in case we get a weapons delivery. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>our <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>and keep the Enfornicators busy.

stages.owner: One of the locals saw a Criminal stashing something in this <Col: StageText>electrical box </Col>as you approached. Your patrol must have spooked him. <Col: StageText>Smash open </Col>that Criminal's stash and take anything you find.
stages.dispatch: We've been sneaking weapons into the city under the Enforcers' noses, but now they're onto us. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>electrical box </Col>that we use as a disguised cache.

stages.owner: A weapons cache? Things just got a little more interesting. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>those <Col: StageText>weapons </Col>back to our <Col: StageText>lock-up </Col>and we'll examine them.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers raided our weapons cache and took a couple of our guns. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>those <Col: StageText>guns </Col>from <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>the Enforcer's <Col: StageText>lock-up</Col>.

stages.owner: Those guns are military-grade, a big cut above the usual weapons we find. We need to locate the source. <Col: StageText>Plant bugs </Col>on <Col: StageText>targets </Col>throughout the block and we'll listen for any useful chatter.
stages.dispatch: The guns that the Enforcers found were only part of our supply. Now they're looking for evidence to lead them to the main stash. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>targets </Col>and stop the Enforcers investigating.

stages.owner: Those Criminals love to talk! We already have information suggesting that guns are smuggled in via unmarked crates. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>the first <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and confiscate the weapons.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and don't let the Enforcers get hold of it and see what's inside. Hint: it isn't cat food. That's our main weapons shipment for the month.

stages.owner: Whoa; that's a LOT of guns. <Col: StageText>Break into </Col>the second <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>all of those guns back to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We need to get those guns out of circulation ASAP.
stages.dispatch: Shit, the Enforcers have half of our weapons shipment. You need to <Col: StageText>protect </Col>our second <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and <Col: StageText>stop </Col>our <Col: StageText>guns </Col>from <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>the Enforcer's <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: With the weapons gone, we have a great opportunity to try and push the Criminals out of this neighborhood. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>.
stages.dispatch: With our weapons gone, we're vulnerable and the Enforcers can move into our turf. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>this <Col: StageText>location</Col>.

stages.owner: We got a call from Paloma Rosario, a CUP city councilor, saying that her baby was kidnapped. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>the <Col: StageText>ransom</Col>, while we work on tracking down the fucker who did this.
stages.dispatch: We've got a lucrative sideline going on: smuggling exotic pets for the San Paro glitterati. But the Enforcers are on to us - <Col: StageText>prevent </Col>the Enforcers <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>our 'pet passport' <Col: StageText>documentation</Col>.

stages.owner: All right, the sick bastard who kidnapped that kid is insisting that we <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location</Col>. Get there fast before this gets out of hand.
stages.dispatch: The 'Forcers got hold of our 'pet passports' - which is gonna make smuggling those twenty-foot albino gators out of Silverfield tricky. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the <Col: StageText>Enforcers collecting </Col>our <Col: StageText>cargo invoices</Col>.

stages.owner: Shit, it looks like the kidnapper got spooked and ran off. Luckily, he dropped his cell phone. <Col: StageText>Pick up </Col>his <Col: StageText>phone </Col>and <Col: StageText>deliver everything </Col>to our <Col: StageText>lockup </Col>- I think we might have a lead.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Enforcers <Col: StageText>delivering </Col>those <Col: StageText>pet passports</Col>. We make too much cash smuggling pets into San Paro to stop now. You know, tiger sharks have a really sweet disposition, once you get to know them.

stages.owner: We got prints from the kidnapper's phone - seems they belong to an ex-con, Vernon Kaig, now living in the area. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>this <Col: StageText>property</Col>; he's been known to hang out there.
stages.dispatch: Shit, the Enforcers are going to raid a couple of our buildings. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the first <Col: StageText>building </Col>and stop the investigation. We have fifty Madagascan fruit bats in there, all wearing diamond collars...

stages.owner: Nothing. Shit, we need to find this kid soon; the first 48 hours are the most important. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>where a couple of Kaig's known associates are based.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers raided our first property, and now they're heading towards the second. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>- don't let them impound our consignment of snow leopard cubs.

stages.owner: That sick fuck! Turns out the kid's been stashed in the kidnapper's vehicle. <Col: StageText>Rescue </Col>the <Col: StageText>child from </Col>the back of this <Col: StageText>van</Col>.
stages.dispatch: We've been using this <Col: StageText>van </Col>to smuggle in these exotic pets for our buyers. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the van from the Enforcers - we've got a blue-throated Gila in there.

stages.owner: Oh, for fuck's sake. A dog? Her "baby" is a dog? San Paro is swarming with crime and Rosario's wasting our time with this? <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>mutt </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. The reward better be worth this bullshit.
stages.dispatch: Damn, that fucking lizard is worth a lot more than you'd think. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the Enforcers before they <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the box to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: Maybe I can forgive the mis-use of our time after all: that crazy councilor paid us well enough. <Col: StageText>Take </Col>the <Col: StageText>cash </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before it gets stolen.

stages.dispatch: Meh. That damn reptile was shitting all over my ride anyway. Enforcers found our sale invoices, though. Either <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>briefcase </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>before the <Col: StageText>Enforcers</Col>.

stages.owner: A website offering Filipino brides has been traced to San Paro, but we're worried it's a cover for something even seedier. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and shut down the website.
stages.dispatch: We've been running a scam website - San Paro Poker - from a building in the area, but Enforcers are looking for our machines. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>housing our dummy networking system.

stages.owner: Damn, no sign of that Filipino brides website. They must be re-routing through a local network. <Col: StageText>Place a packet sniffer on </Col>this <Col: StageText>satellite dish </Col>and we'll be able to trace the wireless signal.
stages.dispatch: We've been re-routing our system wirelessly, but Enforcers are trying to hack our <Col: StageText>telecom dish</Col>. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>it or they'll trace the actual network that runs our scam poker website.

stages.owner: All right - we're close. <Col: StageText>Investigate </Col>the next <Col: StageText>satellite dish </Col>and we should be able to pinpoint the location of that Filipino brides site and shut it down for good.
stages.dispatch: Damn, the Enforcers are getting close. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>telecom dish </Col>or they'll find our computers and shut down our poker website for good.

stages.owner: Good job. It's time to <Col: StageText>raid </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>belonging to SP Web International. Shut down the website and recover any hardware that you can. Hopefully this will help protect those girls.
stages.dispatch: The Enforcers are on their way to our server farm <Col: StageText>building </Col>- <Col: StageText>protect </Col>it from the Enforcer raids or they'll take all of our expensive hardware. If that happens, San Paro Poker is gonna fold.

stages.owner: Whoa. Jackpot. You definitely wouldn't want your mom seeing the pics in there. All right, we need to get those <Col: StageText>computers </Col>back to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>all of them as quickly as you can.
stages.dispatch: Those <Col: StageText>computers </Col>contain a lot of incriminating data - on San Paro Poker, see, the dealer wins 75% of the time. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the computers before the Enforcers get them to their <Col: StageText>lock-up</Col>.

stages.owner: There's a <Col: StageText>laptop </Col>nearby that contains a lot of the transaction data from that Filipino brides website. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>it and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>it away from any opposition.
stages.dispatch: Last chance - we've got wireless incendiaries rigged up inside those machine cases. <Col: StageText>Recover </Col>the <Col: StageText>laptop </Col>used to trigger the devices and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>it away from any opposition.

stages.owner: We've discovered that conflict diamonds are being transported through the docks and then into the rest of the city. <Col: StageText>Search </Col>these <Col: StageText>crates </Col>and confiscate any diamonds that you can find.
stages.dispatch: We make good money sourcing cheap diamonds for the jewelers of San Paro. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these shipping <Col: StageText>crates</Col>. The Praetorians will be looking to raid them and take our merchandise.
