stages.owner: The trade in these conflict diamonds funds war in places that make San Paro look like Candyland. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>those <Col: StageText>diamonds </Col>to the Praetorian <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll shut down these traders for good.
stages.dispatch: The Praetorians have taken some of our diamonds - and we'd already arranged a buyer. If you <Col: StageText>intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>diamonds </Col>before the 'Forcers reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>then we can recover this situation.

stages.owner: Those diamonds were on their way to a jeweler in the city, one who doesn't ask questions. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>the jeweler's <Col: StageText>storeroom </Col>and take anything without the proper import paperwork.
stages.dispatch: Our main jewelry client fears that the Praetorians will be raiding his property next. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the jeweler's <Col: StageText>storeroom </Col>from any raids.

stages.owner: Other jewelers will think twice before buying these conflict diamonds. They don't seem so cheap once you count the cost of us kicking your door in. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>that <Col: StageText>necklace </Col>to our <Col: StageText>evidence store</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Damn, that jeweler is pissed at us. The Praetorians raided his building and took the jewelry we sold him. <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>necklace </Col>before it reaches the Enforcer's <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

stages.owner: We found another crate from the same original shipment. The Criminals are after it already. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and its contents.

stages.dispatch: Our reputation is at stake now. You need to break open this <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and <Col: StageText>take the diamonds</Col>. We can use them to replace the goods our client lost.

stages.owner: You have to <Col: StageText>retrieve </Col>those <Col: StageText>diamonds </Col>before they reach the Criminal <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. If they get away with this, more people will needlessly die digging those rocks out of the ground.

stages.dispatch: All right, now you need to <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>diamonds </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. The Praetorians are gonna be all over you, so try to stay alive.

stages.owner: Judge Mya Singh has hired the Tigers as private security for her daughter's wedding. We can't go empty-handed. <Col: StageText>Search </Col>these <Col: StageText>crates </Col>and take some champagne. It's on its way to the Blood Roses.
stages.dispatch: Our luxury goods import business is going great. Now the Petty Tigers want to steal our latest shipment, probably for themselves. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>our shipping <Col: StageText>crates</Col>.

stages.dispatch: If the Tigers can find one more illegally imported item then a judge will grant search warrants against us. Get to this <Col: StageText>crate </Col>and <Col: StageText>break into</Col> it. We can't be caught with those diamonds.↵

stages.owner: We have to recover that <Col: StageText>evidence</Col>! <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>it before the Criminals reach their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Then take it to Judge Singh, provided she doesn't give it away again!

stages.dispatch: Great, now <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>bag </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. The Tigers will be on your tail - they'd need to catch you in possession of that bag to get their search warrant.

stages.owner: G-King terror attacks have lowered our recruitment rates, and now Teng wants us to win back the hearts and minds of San Paro. <Col: StageText>Paint over graffiti </Col>to help kick-start our publicity drive.
stages.dispatch: Justin Teng's got his Praetorians on an anti-graffiti drive after someone put up a piece advertizing his phone number as a sex hotline. <Col: StageText>Stop the Praetorians </Col>from covering our graffiti.

stages.owner: There's more <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>nearby - keep the <Col: StageText>cover-up </Col>operation going in this neighborhood; we need to show the people we're still alive and kicking. It's all good PR at the end of the day.
stages.dispatch: We've got <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>nearby - <Col: StageText>stop </Col>the Praetorians <Col: StageText>covering it up</Col>. I guess Teng's truly pissed about that graffiti with his phone number on it. Wonder if he got any calls askin' for hot lovin'?

stages.owner: We've got <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>left over in this sector. <Col: StageText>Conceal </Col>this last tag and you're good for now. Hell, you did such a good job I might even recommend you for our next promotional video.
stages.dispatch: Our last <Col: StageText>tag </Col>is nearby. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the tag from Praetorian clean-up squads. Heh, I've done the old 'for a good time' phone number prank before, but the one that riled Teng was three stories tall!

stages.owner: We've got hostiles! Taggers are in the area to reclaim their lost work - <Col: StageText>capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>these locations to keep them out. Show them the Praetorians haven't gone soft.
stages.dispatch: Sucks that the 'Torians managed to cover all our tags; I'll get some taggers to put our colors back up. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>these locations so our taggers can spray up replacement 'fiti safely.

stages.owner: 2iP are doing a piece on the Tigers, but it'll look bad if they come round and find our chapter houses are all graffed up. Do us a favor and <Col: StageText>cover </Col>the crappy <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>up.
stages.dispatch: Heh, the Tigers don't appreciate our tags. Who'd have thought? They've sent some lackeys to clean them up. <Col: StageText>Stop the Tigers </Col>from covering our graffiti.

stages.owner: Awesome. There's <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>nearby - keep up the good work and <Col: StageText>cover over </Col>that one too.
stages.dispatch: We've got <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>nearby - <Col: StageText>stop </Col>the Tigers from <Col: StageText>covering up </Col>our work. Graffiti is art: letting them spray over it just ain't right.

stages.owner: One last piece of <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>we missed over here. <Col: StageText>Spray over </Col>the tag and we're good to go. You fuckin' rock; I owe you a beer for this one.
stages.dispatch: Our last <Col: StageText>tag </Col>claiming the area is close by. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the tag from those Prentiss freaks.

stages.owner: Looks like those tags were new: the dickwads who put them up are back to try and refresh them. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>these locations to keep the taggers out.
stages.dispatch: They got all our tags? Well fuck them then! <Col: StageText>capture </Col>and <Col: StageText>hold </Col>these locations so we can put our graffiti back up.

stages.dispatch: SPPD Internal Affairs is searching for one of our our mole by bugging places where we meet<Col:StageText>Stop them</Col> from planting the bugs.

stages.dispatch: Port Authority plans to seize our weapons shipment as it arrives at the docks. Buy us time to move the guns. First, <Col: StageText>stop </Col>the authorities <Col: StageText>picking up </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>they'll use for the raid.

stages.owner: All right. There's a crate of guns in the marked container. <Col: StageText>Break in </Col>to the <Col: StageText>container</Col> and <Col: StageText>recover the guns</Col>. Knowing Jericho, he probably planned to sell them to the Blood Roses.
stages.dispatch: We managed to get some of the weapons but the rest are being held in this container. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>that <Col: StageText>container</Col>, and don't let those Port Authority idiots get them open.

stages.owner: There's some serious hardware here - Port Authority will want in on this. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>either <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and <Col: StageText>the crate </Col>to the SPPA <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>and we'll get hold of any intelligence they may have.
stages.dispatch: The SPPA are taking those <Col: StageText>weapons </Col>and <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>nearby. You need to <Col: StageText>stop </Col>those deliveries and take back our arsenal.

stages.owner: Good. Now <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>our second <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>to our own <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. We'll get them out of circulation before Jericho even knows they're missing.
stages.dispatch: The <Col: StageText>weapons </Col>and one of the <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>have been delivered. Port Authority is taking the rest to a second <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>, not far from the first. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>that delivery.

stages.owner: We're working with the Port Authority to trace the smuggling route Jericho used. Go back and <Col: StageText>capture </Col>this <Col: StageText>crime scene</Col>. If any of Jericho's men turn up, don't let them take back the scene.
stages.dispatch: The SPPA may have taken those weapons, but if we control the docks, we can bring in more. Get back and <Col: StageText>capture </Col>this <Col: StageText>location</Col>.

stages.owner: Get a feel for how strong the Enforcers are around here. They hate <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col>, so go <Col: StageText>spray</Col> some up and get their attention, Blood Rose style!
stages.dispatch: Street intel says the Blood Roses are out <Col: StageText>tagging</Col> up the area. <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> their mindless vandalism.

stages.owner: Sweet! Look at all that paint. Bet they don't want to see the Roses ruling this area. <Col: StageText>Spray</Col> one more <Col: StageText>wall</Col> for good measure.
stages.dispatch: <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> those Blood Rose vandals. Take a gun and explain, in real small, bullet-sized words, that we don't consider <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col> to be an art form.

stages.owner: Stupid 'Forcers fell for it, and you can easily take out those few losers. <Col: StageText>Capture this area</Col>. Send a message that this is Blood Rose turf.
stages.dispatch: It's an ambush! <Col: StageText>Capture the area</Col> and take out these wannabe paint jockeys.

stages.owner: The 'Forcers sneak around this neighborhood like a bunch of schoolgirls playing hookey. Draw them out into the open by <Col: StageText>spraying</Col> some <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col>.
stages.dispatch: Got a street patrol saying those skater-punk G-Kings are spraying <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col> all over our fair city. <Col: StageText>Prevent</Col> this vandalism.

stages.owner: They ain't gonna like the the G-Kings being so bold! <Col: StageText>Spray</Col> one more <Col: StageText>wall</Col> for good measure.
stages.dispatch: The G-Kings are like tomcats pissing around to mark their territory. <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> them spraying their stinking <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col> on the walls.

stages.owner: Dumb Enforcers fell for it. <Col: StageText>Capture the area</Col>and show no mercy. See how they like going toe to toe with the G-Kings!
stages.dispatch: Looks like they want to fight. Rub their noses in it! <Col: StageText>Capture the area</Col>.
